question: Can I use the physical presence calculator before creating an online account to apply for citizenship?

hits.title: Apply for citizenship: Calculate your physical presence
hits.text:
Apply for citizenship: Calculate your physical presence
Answer the following question to learn how to calculate your physical presence (opens in a new tab) .
Online application
The calculator is now available in the online account (opens in a new tab) .
- You can only use the calculator after you create your account.
- To do your calculation, follow the instructions in the “ Physical presence calculator ” section of the online account.
Before you apply online, you can check if you have at least 1,095 days of physical presence with the calculator for paper application (opens in a new tab) .
You must still use the calculator in your account to apply online.

hits.title: Apply for citizenship: Calculate your physical presence
hits.text:
Track your time with the travel journal (optional)
You may use our travel journal to record your trips outside Canada.
- This helps you calculate how many days you’ve been in Canada.
- You don’t need to include the travel journal in your application.
Get the travel journal (opens in a new tab)
Paper application
You have 2 options to do your calculation:
Option 1: Use the online physical presence calculator (recommended)
How to use the online calculator:
- Fill out the calculator.
- Print your completed calculation.
- Include the calculation printout in your application.
Go to the calculator (opens in a new tab)
Option 2: Complete the CIT 0407 form
If you can’t or don’t want to use the online physical presence calculator
- fill out and print this form: How to Calculate Physical Presence (CIT 0407) (opens in new tab)
- include the completed form in your application

hits.title: Search of citizenship records: How to apply
hits.text:
Start your online application
In the account
- we’ll check if you can apply online
- you can apply online urgently if you qualify
Once you start your online application, you have 60 days to submit it.
The online application works best in Google Chrome.
Create an account or sign in
Apply on paper for your or someone else’s records
If you’ve already applied online, do not apply on paper for the same request. If you do, we won’t process your paper application.
Get the application package
The application package has the instruction guide and the form you must fill out.
- Read the instruction guide carefully before you complete the form.
- If information or documents are missing , it may delay the processing of your application.

hits.title: Search of citizenship records: How to apply
hits.text:
How to apply online urgently
We’ll ask you if you need urgent processing in the online application.
Answer “Yes” and:
- explain why you need urgent processing
- upload documents to support your explanation, for example
- a letter from a foreign government stating that they need the information
- a letter from an employer
We’ll review your request to see if it qualifies. Even if you qualify, we can’t guarantee that you’ll get your search of citizenship record on time.
Before you start
To apply online, you need
- to read the instruction guide to apply online (opens in a new tab)
- an email address
- access to a scanner or digital camera
- a valid credit card or Canadian debit card to pay online when you submit your application
- a printer to print your result letter, if you want

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for stateless people: Submit your application
hits.text:
Mail your application
To avoid delays or a return of your application package, follow these steps before you mail it.
- Before you sign the form
- Confirm you still meet the citizenship eligibility requirements.
- Check completeness
- Confirm that you have included every required form, document and payment receipt.
- If applying as a family or a group, put all complete applications and receipts in one envelope so that we can process them together.
- If any application is incomplete, we will return the entire package
- Sign and date the form
- Sign the application form yourself.
- Use the actual date you sign the form. Do not back-date or post-date.
- The date you sign your application form must be the date you enter in the physical presence calculation section (section 9, line B).
- Send the package right away
- Courier or mail the application package within 90 days of the signature date.

- a valid credit card or Canadian debit card to pay online when you submit your application
- a printer to print your result letter, if you want

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for stateless people: Submit your application
hits.text:
Mail your application
To avoid delays or a return of your application package, follow these steps before you mail it.
- Before you sign the form
- Confirm you still meet the citizenship eligibility requirements.
- Check completeness
- Confirm that you have included every required form, document and payment receipt.
- If applying as a family or a group, put all complete applications and receipts in one envelope so that we can process them together.
- If any application is incomplete, we will return the entire package
- Sign and date the form
- Sign the application form yourself.
- Use the actual date you sign the form. Do not back-date or post-date.
- The date you sign your application form must be the date you enter in the physical presence calculation section (section 9, line B).
- Send the package right away
- Courier or mail the application package within 90 days of the signature date.

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for minor 5(1) : Forms and documents to apply on paper
hits.text:
Required documents
You must provide all of the following forms and documents. You can open each one to get more details.
Document checklist
Download and complete the document checklist (Cit 0560) (opens in a new tab) .
Include the completed checklist with the mailed application.
Application form
Download and complete the citizenship application form for minor 5(1) (Cit 0403) (opens in a new tab) .
The minor’s physical presence calculation
Find out how to provide the minor’s physical presence calculation (opens in a new tab) .

question: Can I take the citizenship test in person or with Microsoft Teams if I have a weak Internet connection?

hits.title: Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
hits.text:
If you cannot take the test online
We may invite you to take the test in person or with Microsoft Teams if you
- have a weak or unreliable Internet connection
- have no access to an electronic device or webcam
- cannot use the supported browsers for the test (Chrome or Safari)
Face covering (online test)
Your face must be fully visible through your webcam during the online test.
We may invite you to take the test in person or with Microsoft Teams if you can’t remove your face covering.
Ceremony accommodations
We may invite you to a virtual or an in-person ceremony.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
If you’re taking the test in person or on Microsoft Teams
If you take the test in person or on Microsoft Teams, your invitation will include the details, for example, the time and location. If you fail the test, you’ll get a new invitation for another time.
How to reschedule the test
If you need to reschedule the test, email the address in the rescheduling section of your test invitation. In your email, include
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule your test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to reschedule your test, but it may take longer.
Urgent processing for emergencies
If you need to take the test before the 30-day period on your invitation due to an emergency, check if you qualify for urgent processing .

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Microsoft Teams help
If you need help with Microsoft Teams, contact the office that sent you the test invitation by replying to your invitation email. In your email, include
- a detailed explanation of how you need help
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
If you closed the test by mistake
If you closed the test by mistake, sign in again as soon as possible.
Even if you left in the middle of your test, the 45-minute timer will continue . When 45 minutes have passed, the system will automatically submit your test with any answers you selected.
If you’re not able to complete the test due to technical issues or emergencies, you may have to
- do an interview with our officer
- retake the test by videoconference, if necessary

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Take the online test
After you receive the invitation, you can take the online citizenship test. Find out what you need to do to prepare for and complete the test.
This page doesn’t apply to the other test formats (in person or on Microsoft Teams).
Getting ready for the test
Citizenship tests are 45 minutes long. Once the timer starts, you won’t be able to stop it. After 45 minutes, your test will be submitted automatically, even if you’re not finished. You’ll get a warning when you have 5 minutes left.
Before you start the test, make sure you’re prepared.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Test results and next steps
hits.text:
Official test result
For tests taken in person and on Microsoft Teams , you’ll get your official test score right after you take the test.
After you take the online test , one of our officers will review your result to make it official. This could take a few days or a few weeks. There are 3 possible test results:
Pass
You correctly answered at least 15 of the 20 questions (75%).
Fail
You failed all your test attempts during the 30-day period in your invitation.
Invalidated
Your test result may be invalid if
- we find out or suspect that you cheated
- a technical issue prevents us from confirming your identity or your test score

question: Can I request a waiver for the oath of citizenship and the test or language requirements for an adult with a mental disability who doesn't have a guardian or a representative?

hits.title: Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
hits.text:
Option 1 (recommended): Reply to your invitation
Reply to the office that sent you the invitation.
Option 2: Send us a web form
You can also request an accommodation by sending us a web form .
If you need a waiver (exemption)
If you have a situation that prevents you from meeting a requirement, you can request a waiver instead of an accommodation. You can request a waiver for these requirements:
- Citizenship test and language requirement: Your situation must meet the waiver criteria .
- Oath of citizenship : We’ll only give a waiver if a mental disability (like an intellectual or a developmental disability) prevents an applicant from understanding the oath.
- For example, they don’t understand that taking the oath makes them a Canadian citizen.
If we approve your waiver request, you don’t need to meet the requirement (for example, you don’t need to take the test).
Learn more about the waiver

hits.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements: after you submit your request
hits.text:
If we refuse your waiver request
We’ll send you a letter to let you know if we refuse a request.
You must take the test, prove your language skills or take the oath (depending on the waiver you asked for).
If you need help meeting these requirements, you can request an accommodation for accessibility or another reason .

hits.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements: after you submit your request
hits.text:
After you submit your waiver request
After we get your request, we’ll
- review it to make sure that you qualify for the waiver
- tell you our decision or ask for more information
We can’t guarantee the approval of a waiver request. Our officers will review all requests on a case-by-case basis.
If we approve your waiver request
You do not need to take the test, prove your language skills or take the oath of citizenship (depending on the waiver of you asked for).
If you check your application status , these sections of the status tracker will have a “ Waived ” status (where applicable):
- Citizenship test
- Language skills
- Citizenship ceremony

hits.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements
hits.text:
Waiver for citizenship requirements
To become a Canadian citizen, you must meet certain requirements when you apply. If you can’t meet a specific requirement, you can request an exemption. This is called a waiver. If your waiver is approved, it means you don’t need to meet that requirement.
You can only request a waiver for
- the citizenship test
- proving your English or French language skills
- the oath of citizenship
If you can meet the requirement but you need help with it , request an accommodation instead .

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for minor 5(1) : Forms and documents to apply on paper
hits.text:
Waiver (exemption) documents
You can request a waiver (exemption) if the minor
- is between 14 and 17 years old when signing the application
- can’t take the oath of citizenship at the citizenship ceremony (for example, due to a disability or other accessibility reasons)
If we approve the waiver request, the minor doesn’t have to take the oath of citizenship.
How to get the waiver documents
- Check if the minor qualifies for a waiver (opens in a new tab) .
- If they qualify, answer some questions to get the right documents (opens in a new tab) .
For more information

question: How do I request to host a citizenship ceremony?

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
hits.text:
How to host a ceremony
Explore the steps, guidelines and best practices that will help you host a memorable citizenship ceremony.
Steps to host a ceremony
- Contact us What to include in your request
Contact us
If you’re interested in hosting a citizenship ceremony, submit your hosting request by
- email , or
- mail to your closest Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) office
To avoid delays, send your request only once .
What to include in your request
- Use the subject line in your email or letter: “Citizenship Ceremony Hosting Request – [Proposed date]”
- Tell us in English or French :
- name of your organization
- brief description of your organization
- contact person’s name, telephone and email
- type of citizenship ceremony you’d like to host (in-person or virtual)
- proposed dates for the ceremony
- for an in-person ceremony , also include:
- proposed venue
- room capacity (ideally large enough to accommodate candidates and their guests)

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
hits.text:
Stage 3: 14 days before the ceremony
With 2 weeks to go, it’s time to finalize the schedule and confirm all arrangements.
- Review the detailed sequence of events prepared by the clerk of the ceremony.
- Confirm any special arrangements for guest speakers, performances, music or entertainment, such as smudging ceremonies or security requirements.
- Review the host representative’s remarks with IRCC staff.
- Address any special requests from participants.
- Prepare a news release.
- Invite media outlets.
- Finalize the reception menu , considering dietary restrictions.
- Start media promotion, if applicable.
- Consider attending an in-person ceremony if you’re unfamiliar with how a ceremony unfolds.

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
hits.text:
- In some cases, IRCC may approve the special guest list and authorize the host to send the invitations.
- Arrange entertainment, performers or a musical interlude, if applicable.
- Confirm any special venue arrangements, such as how ceremony participants and IRCC officials will access venues that charge admission.
- If an Indigenous participant is involved and you, as the host, are working directly with them, coordinate the following:
- any ceremony requirements such as smudging, introductions and offerings
- preferences for receiving ceremonial items
- their profile for introduction by the presiding official
- Provide the local IRCC office with client-facing information (such as parking information, building access, directions) for inclusion in ceremony invitations.
- Plan the layout of the venue: chairs, stage, podium, tables, green room, registration and reception area.
- Decide if a news release is needed.
- Plan the reception (optional).

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
hits.text:
Do
- have a detailed and organized plan
- consult with IRCC staff at every stage of planning
- welcome all cultures in your community
- show sensitivity to community issues
- choose a venue that is appropriate for the theme of citizenship
- cover or remove any signage or symbols that reference alcohol, advertising or religion
- select a venue or location that the general public can access
- keep local IRCC staff informed by copying them on emails to special guests (if applicable)
- for all ceremonies (regardless of language format):
- have at least 1 bilingual staff or volunteer present at the ceremony or direct ceremony guest to a bilingual IRCC official
- host staff and volunteers must actively offer services in both official languages to new citizens and their guests whenever possible. If the host can’t provide enough bilingual support, you must inform IRCC staff.
- for predominantly 1-language ceremonies (mostly English or mostly French):

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: How to host a ceremony
hits.text:
Work with us to plan the ceremony
We’ll respond to your hosting request so we can start planning the ceremony together. The handy checklists below show what you can expect:
Stage 1: 45 days before the ceremony
Start preparations early to ensure a smooth event.
IRCC staff will take your suggestions into account, but ceremony details will only be finalized once officially confirmed by IRCC.
- Finalize the ceremony’s date and venue .
Things to keep in mind
- Have a backup plan in case rescheduling is needed.
- Be mindful of any possible cultural or religious observances related to the chosen date.
- Meet with us in person, virtually or by phone.

question: How do I request to host a citizenship ceremony?

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: Guidelines and resources
hits.text:
Hosts
- Hosts of non-profit organizations may display 1 or 2 bilingual banners of their organization at the back of the ceremony room or in the hallway near the reception area.
- Hosts may set up a table or kiosk featuring bilingual materials about their organization and programs.
- This must be placed at the back of the room or outside of the ceremony room, ideally in the reception area.
- IRCC will determine what’s permitted based on available space.
- Host representatives must stay at their table or kiosk.
- Hosts may not actively distribute materials at the table or kiosk—new citizens or guests must approach them voluntarily.
- Sports teams or other multicultural centres acting as hosts can request a checklist with advertising dos and don’ts from IRCC.

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: Guidelines and resources
hits.text:
Indigenous participants
If an Indigenous participant will be present at the citizenship ceremony, check with your local IRCC office before the event to confirm whether any parts of Indigenous teachings should not be photographed or recorded. This may include smudging, blessings or other ceremonial elements.
Livestreaming
If you want to livestream a citizenship ceremony, talk to IRCC first. IRCC officials need to inform all ceremony participants in advance.
Tips
- Record or livestream only the ceremony itself (for example, from the official opening to the platform party’s exit).
- Don’t include the preamble or post-ceremony instructions.
- You may photograph or record the reception, if there is one.

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: When and where to host a ceremony
hits.text:
When and where to host a ceremony
Explore key considerations for choosing the right time and place for the citizenship ceremony you’re hosting.
When to host a ceremony
Ceremonies can be held in the morning, afternoon or early evening. To ensure smooth coordination:
- You must consult with IRCC staff to avoid scheduling conflicts.
- Weekday ceremonies are usually done during regular business hours.
- Weekend ceremonies may be arranged for special occasions.
- Statutory holidays are generally avoided, with the exception of Canada Day.
- If you’d like an elected official to attend, check their availability using the appropriate government sitting calendar. Let your IRCC office know and we’ll send the invitation.
Ceremony duration may vary, depending on the number of invited candidates and if there’s a reception. More timing details are available upon request.

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: Guidelines and resources
hits.text:
Working with the media (in-person ceremony only)
Media coverage can help highlight the significance of citizenship ceremonies. But it must be coordinated carefully to respect participants and maintain the integrity of the event.
Host responsibilities
Before involving media, hosts must
- consult with IRCC staff before sending any media invitations
- ensure media representatives understand they must use their own permission release forms when interviewing new citizens
- prepare designated interview areas at the ceremony venue
- confirm there are enough electrical outlets for media equipment
- discuss whether media risers are required for filming or photography
- inform IRCC staff or IRCC media relations of any concerns regarding media presence at the ceremony

hits.title: Host a citizenship ceremony: Guidelines and resources
hits.text:
What your posters or materials must not include
They must not
- include the IRCC or Government of Canada logo
- include the names or photos of presiding officials or special guests
- be displayed in ceremony spaces (lobby, registration, room itself, reception)
Optional information
Your posters or materials may include
- the host’s logo
- sponsor names or logos at the bottom of the poster
- If you include sponsors, clearly state their role. For example, “sponsor of the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada citizenship ceremony hosted by [host name].”

question: Do I need to fill out the Residence Outside of Canada form (CIT 0177) for my child who lived abroad with me as a family member of a Crown servant during the eligibility period for Canadian citizenship?

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for minor 5(1) : Forms and documents to apply on paper
hits.text:
Residence outside Canada with a Crown servant (Cit 0177)
If the minor spent time outside Canada as a family member of a Crown servant during their eligibility period, download and complete the Residence Outside of Canada form (CIT 0177) (opens in a new tab) .
The eligibility period is 5 years before the date the application is signed.
- It covers the time when the minor has been a permanent resident (PR).
- If the minor has been a PR for less than 5 years, the eligibility period includes the entire time they’ve held the PR status.
A Crown servant
- is a person employed in or with the Canadian Armed Forces, the federal public administration or the public service of a province or territory
- doesn’t include locally engaged employees (foreign citizens hired in their own countries by the Canadian government to support Canadian offices abroad)
A family member of a Crown servant includes their
- child
- spouse
- common law partner

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
hits.text:
Permanent resident minors: You need to apply for the child’s Canadian citizenship
To get a citizenship certificate, you must apply for the child to become a Canadian citizen (opens in a new tab) .
- If we approve the application, they’ll get the certificate after the citizenship ceremony (opens in a new tab) .
- Do not apply directly for a citizenship certificate (online or on paper). If you do, we’ll return your application.
Getting a certificate for the first time: You can’t apply together with an adopted child who was born outside Canada
You cannot apply for yourself and an adopted child (under 18) born outside Canada at the same time (online or on paper).

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
hits.text:
If you were born and adopted outside Canada
If you were born outside Canada and adopted by a Canadian parent, you’re not automatically a Canadian citizen.
Before submitting an application, learn about citizenship by descent for adopted people .
Minors who are permanent residents
If your minor child is a permanent resident, you will likely need to apply for your child’s Canadian citizenship (naturalization or grant of citizenship) to get a citizenship certificate.
If you apply to become a Canadian citizen
If you apply for and receive Canadian citizenship ( naturalization or grant of citizenship ), you
- will receive the certificate at a citizenship ceremony
- do not need to apply for a citizenship certificate

Details to know when you fill out your form
You must type the code PPTR2PRQC2026 in the Job Title field of the IMM 5710 or IMM1295 form.
If you’re applying to restore your status
Using the same form, you can
- apply to get a work permit
- restore your status
In the first section of the form, under question 3, “I am applying for one or more of the following:” choose “Restore my status as a worker.”

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
hits.text:
If you were born and adopted outside Canada
If you were born outside Canada and adopted by a Canadian parent, you’re not automatically a Canadian citizen.
Before submitting an application, learn about citizenship by descent for adopted people .
Minors who are permanent residents
If your minor child is a permanent resident, you will likely need to apply for your child’s Canadian citizenship (naturalization or grant of citizenship) to get a citizenship certificate.
If you apply to become a Canadian citizen
If you apply for and receive Canadian citizenship ( naturalization or grant of citizenship ), you
- will receive the certificate at a citizenship ceremony
- do not need to apply for a citizenship certificate

hits.title: A family member of someone who applied for permanent residence needs a work permit
hits.text:
You need a work permit A family member of someone who applied for permanent residence needs a work permit
If you’re a family member who has been included in an application for permanent residence, you need a work permit to work in Canada.
You may be eligible for an open work permit if you’ve been included in one of the following applications for permanent residence that has been found complete or has received a positive eligibility assessment:
- Agri-Food Pilot
- Atlantic Immigration Program
- Canadian experience class
- caring for children class or caring for people with high medical needs class
- federal skilled trades class
- federal skilled worker class
- Francophone Community Immigration Pilot (FCIP)
- holders of a Quebec Selection Certificate (CSQ) who applied for PR including
- Quebec skilled worker class
- Quebec investors program
- Home Child-Care Provider Pilot and Home Support Worker Pilot – Direct to PR stream
- Provincial Nominee Program

hits.title: Resume Canadian citizenship: After you apply
hits.text:
- The e-certificate will be available in the IRCC Portal within 5 business days of our receipt of your signed Oath or Affirmation of Citizenship form.
Learn more about the citizenship certificate (opens in a new tab)

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: About the process
hits.text:
We stopped issuing citizenship cards
We no longer give out citizenship cards – archived or the commemorative certificates that came with them. If you apply to update or replace your citizenship card, we will send you a citizenship certificate.
Fees
Proof of citizenship (citizenship certificate): $75
Processing time ?
We couldn’t load the data. Try again.
Applications outside Canada and the United States may take longer .
Processing times for applications outside Canada and the United States
Add 3 to 4 months to account for mailing time if you
- live outside Canada and the U.S. and
- are applying through a Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate
Add 6 to 8 months to processing time if you
- are applying for a minor (under 18) who lives outside Canada and the U.S. and
- sent the application directly to the Case Processing Centre in Sydney, Nova Scotia

hits.title: Resume Canadian citizenship: After you apply
hits.text:
Once your application is received at the Case Processing Centre in Sydney, Nova Scotia, it will be reviewed and we will start processing it.
Some applications may encounter delays. For example, if documents are missing or if your case is complex, we may contact you to get more information or to ask you to send us additional information. Such cases may take longer to process.
To find out how long it takes to process applications to resume your Canadian citizenship, see processing times . You can check the status of your application on line .
If you cannot see the status of your application online, and the normal processing times have passed, you may contact us by using this Web form .
You may have to be interviewed by a citizenship officer. If so, we will notify you by mail of the time and place of your interview.
If we approve your application
- we’ll invite you to take the oath of citizenship at the citizenship ceremony
- you’ll receive a Canadian citizenship certificate

hits.title: Resume Canadian citizenship: How to apply
hits.text:
Submit your application
Mail your completed application form and the required documents to
Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada Case Processing Centre – Sydney Resumption P.O. Box 10000 Sydney, Nova Scotia B1P 7C1
If your application is signed more than three months before we receive it or if it is dated into the future, we will send it back to you.
Track your application
Track your application
We recommend that you use a postal or courier service that provides a tracking number so you can confirm delivery to IRCC.

Some applications may take longer to process
- If documents or fees (if applicable) are missing, we will return your application to you.

Check the status of your application online . If the normal processing times have passed and you cannot check the status of your application online, you can send us an enquiry by using this Web form .
A citizenship officer may need to interview you
If so, we’ll notify you by mail of the time and place of your interview.
- If you live outside Canada, the Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate responsible for your area will contact you to let you know how the interview will be conducted.
- If you need to change your appointment, contact the office that sent you the invitation.
- The contact information is in the letter we sent you.
You may withdraw your application . If you do, you may be eligible for a refund .

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for stateless people: Submit your application
hits.text:
Mail your application
To avoid delays or a return of your application package, follow these steps before you mail it.
- Before you sign the form
- Confirm you still meet the citizenship eligibility requirements.
- Check completeness
- Confirm that you have included every required form, document and payment receipt.
- If applying as a family or a group, put all complete applications and receipts in one envelope so that we can process them together.
- If any application is incomplete, we will return the entire package
- Sign and date the form
- Sign the application form yourself.
- Use the actual date you sign the form. Do not back-date or post-date.
- The date you sign your application form must be the date you enter in the physical presence calculation section (section 9, line B).
- Send the package right away
- Courier or mail the application package within 90 days of the signature date.

hits.title: Search of citizenship records: After you apply
hits.text:
To ask for urgent processing of your submitted application , contact the Canadian embassy, consulate or high commission (opens in a new tab) where you submitted your application.
We’ll review your request to see if it qualifies. Even if you qualify, we can’t guarantee that you’ll get your search of citizenship record on time.
Get your search result
We’ll mail your letter to the embassy, high commission or consulate where you submitted your application.
- It’s valid for 1 year .
- If the person whose record you searched for is deceased, the letter doesn’t expire.

question: How can I download individual e-certificates if I applied as a family or group with one email address?

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
If you applied as a family or a group with 1 email address
To download the individual e-certificates, provide the following information for each person on the “Download Citizenship e-Certificate” page of the IRCC Portal:
- application number (opens in a new tab) .
- unique client identifier (UCI) (opens in a new tab) .
- date of birth
You don’t have the download instructions letter
We send the letter to the last email address you gave us . This may be the one that
- you put on your online application or paper application form
- you provided after you applied (for example, by using our web form to update your information)
You should
- check for a message from an email address ending in “@cic.gc.ca”
- check your spam or junk folder
If you still can’t find the instructions letter
- you can request a new code
- you need to use a different email from the one you applied with

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
If you applied for citizenship online
The IRCC Portal is different from the account where you submitted your application.
That’s why you need to create a new account to download your e-certificate.
If you already have an IRCC Portal account
You can sign in to download your e-certificate .
If you applied as a family or group with 1 email address
You can download all e-certificates in the same IRCC Portal account .
If you applied to become a Canadian citizen or resume your citizenship
We send the letter with the instructions on how to download the e-certificate after you’ve attended the ceremony and submitted your signed Oath or Affirmation of Citizenship form (you’ll get the form in the ceremony invitation or at the ceremony).
You will receive the letter by e-mail within 5 business days of our receipt of your signed Oath or Affirmation of Citizenship form.

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
Email address for e-certificate download
The last email address you gave us may be the one that
- you put on your online application or paper application form
- you provided after you applied (for example, by using our web form to update your information)
If you applied online
When you create an IRCC Portal account, your password must be unique to the account.
You cannot reuse your
- password for your online citizenship application account (if you applied to become a Canadian citizen)
- GCKey or Sign-In Partner information for your IRCC secure account (if you applied for a citizenship certificate)

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
Online application for a citizenship certificate (proof of citizenship)
In most cases, you’ll get the letter in your IRCC secure account .
- If you asked us to communicate with you through email after you applied, we’ll send the letter to the last email address you gave us .
- If you applied with the help of a representative, we’ll email them the letter .
If you applied with the help of a representative
Your representative will receive the letter with instructions on how to download your e-certificate.
To download your e-certificate without going through your representative, use this page to create your own IRCC Portal account .
You may still ask your representative to forward you the instructions letter.
- Do not use the invite code in the letter. You must request a new invitation code using your own email in the IRCC portal.
- The letter has other helpful information about your e-certificate, such as where in the IRCC Portal you can download the file.

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
View and download your e-certificate
Unlike a paper certificate, you can download the e-certificate instead of waiting for us to mail it to you.
Follow these steps to view and download your e-certificate:
If we approve your application, we’ll give you a letter with instructions on how to download the certificate. How you receive the letter depends on what you applied for.
Most citizenship applications
This includes
- online and paper applications to become a Canadian citizen
- paper applications for a citizenship certificate (proof of citizenship)
- applications to resume Canadian citizenship after giving it up (paper application only)
If you applied for any of the above, we’ll send the letter to the last email address you gave us .

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for Stateless people: Wait for a decision
hits.text:
- plan to leave Canada for more than 2 weeks in a row
- can’t check your application status online, and the normal processing time for your application has passed
- are charged with a crime
- applied as part of a group but now want to continue the application by yourself
- want to update any other information in your application
If you don’t update us
- it may take us longer to process your application or
- we may refuse or abandon (stop processing) your application
Due to privacy laws, we can’t give information about your application to anyone unless you consent in writing . For example, if you have difficulty communicating in English or French, you need to provide consent for a family member to contact us about your application.

Travel document details

A minor 5(2) applicant
- is under 18 years old when the application is signed

- Do not apply directly for a citizenship certificate (online or on paper). If you do, we’ll return your application.

question: How do I start the citizenship test after receiving an invitation?

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
How to start the test
- Sign in
- Sign in to the online test only after you receive an invitation.
- Use your application number and your unique client identifier (UCI) to sign in.
- Read and accept the privacy notice, and the terms and conditions.
- Request the test link and check your email
- Select the “Email me the test link” button at the bottom of the page. We’ll send the link to the same email address that received the test invitation (the email on your citizenship application) or your representative’s email.
- If you’re using a representative, you’ll have an option to send the link to your email instead of theirs.
- It may take a few minutes for you or your representative to receive the test link.
- The link expires after 15 minutes. If your link expires, sign in again to get a new test link.
- If you sent yourself a test link multiple times, use the latest test link to sign in.
- Confirm your identity
- Re-enter your application number and UCI to confirm your identity.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Take the online test
After you receive the invitation, you can take the online citizenship test. Find out what you need to do to prepare for and complete the test.
This page doesn’t apply to the other test formats (in person or on Microsoft Teams).
Getting ready for the test
Citizenship tests are 45 minutes long. Once the timer starts, you won’t be able to stop it. After 45 minutes, your test will be submitted automatically, even if you’re not finished. You’ll get a warning when you have 5 minutes left.
Before you start the test, make sure you’re prepared.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Changing the email that receives the test link
If you want to change your email address before you receive the invitation, use our web form .
If you want to change your email address after you receive the invitation
If you’ve already received your invitation, email the address in your invitation, and include your application number and unique client identifier (UCI).
It will take time for us to update your email. Continue to check your previous email address.
If you have a representative but want the test link sent to your email, follow these instructions:
- Login to the online test.
- Select the “Email me the test link” button, and you’ll see the option to update the email address.
- Select “Yes, I want to use my email address (new email),” and provide the required information.
- You’ll need to know your representative’s email; this should be the email they used to forward your invitation to you.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
Wait for a test invitation
You need an invitation to take the test online.
What’s on the invitation
We’ll send you an invitation by email to take the online test after you submit your citizenship application. The test invitation is a PDF attachment in an email. The PDF includes instructions on what to do before, during and after the test.
Your invitation should have
- a test start date and end date (you’ll have 30 days to take it)
- a link to the test (or directions for an in-person test)
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
- an email address you can use to contact us

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
When you can take the test
If you take the test online , you can take your test only between the start date and end date provided on your invitation. This will be a 30-day period.
After you receive your invitation, you
- have up to 3 chances to pass the test during the 30-day period
- If you fail, log in and try again to use your chances.
- can take the test at any time during the 30-day period (including weekends and holidays)
You can’t sign in to the test
- before or after the 30-day period on your invitation or
- after you submit the test

Quality Assurance Program
Our Quality Assurance Program randomly selects applications for a detailed review. If your application is selected, we’ll

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for Stateless people: Wait for a decision
hits.text:
Wait for a decision
Learn what happens after you submit your application and how you can track its status.
What happens first
When the Case Processing Centre in Sydney (CPC Sydney) receives your application, the staff there will check that you
- included all the required documents
- paid the correct fees
If your application is complete , we’ll start processing your application and send you an acknowledgement of receipt letter.
If your application is incomplete or missing fees, we’ll return your application to you.
After the initial review, CPC Sydney sends your application to a local IRCC office to make a final decision. You may be asked to attend an interview with a citizenship officer or a citizenship judge.

You can apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate if you

hits.title: Search of citizenship records: How to apply
hits.text:
Search of citizenship records: How to apply
- 1. About the process
- 2. How to apply
- 3. After you apply
Before you apply, make sure you’re eligible for a search of citizenship records.
Apply online to get your own records
You can apply online only to get your own records . To get someone else’s record , you need to apply on paper .
If you’ve already applied on paper, do not apply online for the same request. If you do, we won’t process your online application.
If you need to apply online urgently
We can process applications faster than our normal processing times in special cases , such as
- confirming to a foreign government that you’re not a citizen (for example, to get a passport from that country)
- administering the estate of a deceased person or executing a will
- showing you are (or are not) a citizen to get a certain job

hits.title: Resume Canadian citizenship: After you apply
hits.text:
If we approve your application
- we’ll invite you to take the oath of citizenship at the citizenship ceremony
- you’ll receive a Canadian citizenship certificate
You may withdraw your application . If you do, you may be eligible for a refund .

question: What should I do if I see a blank screen or a message that my browser isn’t supported when taking the citizenship test?

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Blank screen or message that browser isn’t supported
If you see a blank screen or a message that your browser isn’t supported, make sure you’re using Chrome or Safari .
If you’re already using Chrome or Safari, try
- updating your Chrome or Safari to the latest version
- disabling your browser extensions
- clearing your browser’s cookies and cache
- turning off hardware acceleration and restarting the browser (if you use Chrome)
- restarting your browser or device
- reinstalling your browser and keeping all the default settings
- using a different device to take the test
If you still have issues signing in, email the address in your test invitation.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
403 error message
If you get a 403 error message when you sign in, try
- turning off your virtual private network (VPN)
- disabling your browser extensions
- using a different device
- using a different Internet connection
- waiting a few hours to take the test
If you still have issues signing in, email the address in your test invitation.
“You can’t take the test right now” message
You may see this message if you
- attempted to sign in
- before you got your test invitation
- before or after your 30-day period of test access
- entered the wrong application number or unique client identifier (UCI)
If you still have issues signing in, email the address in your test invitation.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Webcam can’t connect to the online test system
If your webcam isn’t working and can’t connect to the online test system, find help related to using
- the Chrome browser
- You can’t take the test with Chrome on an iPad at this time.
- the Chrome operating system (OS) and Chromebook
- the Mac OS and Safari browser
- Windows 7
- Windows 8
- Windows 10
- Windows 11
- a tablet
Fixing webcam issues in a tablet
Option 1
- Close all other applications and web pages that you won’t use for the test.
- Click “ ok ” if you see an error message on the test web page or refresh the page.
- Sign in to the test again (opens in a new tab)
Option 2
- Reset or restart your tablet.
- Sign in to the test again (opens in a new tab)
If your webcam is working , but it can’t connect to the online test system, you may see this error message:
Follow these steps:
- Try using a different device to take the test.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
If you don’t receive the test link
It may take a few minutes for you or your representative to receive the test link. To see if you received it, check
- for messages from an email address ending in “@cic.gc.ca”
- your email junk or spam folder
If you don’t get the test link and your representative doesn’t either, follow these steps:
- Check your spam or junk folder.
- Add the test link email address to your “safe senders” list: notifications@ct-tc.apps.cic.gc.ca .
- Request the link again by clicking on the “Resend the test link” button.
- Make sure you’re using Chrome or Safari, and turn off any virtual private networks (VPNs).
If you still don’t get the test link, email the address in your test invitation and include
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
If your webcam is working , but it can’t connect to the online test system, you may see this error message:
Follow these steps:
- Try using a different device to take the test.
- If you can’t return to the test within 45 minutes, email the address in your test invitation and include
- a detailed explanation of the issue and how you tried to fix it
- whether you have a different device to take the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
We’ll reschedule your test once we’ve reviewed your email. It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to reschedule your test, but it may take longer.

hits.title: Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
hits.text:
If you cannot take the test online
We may invite you to take the test in person or with Microsoft Teams if you
- have a weak or unreliable Internet connection
- have no access to an electronic device or webcam
- cannot use the supported browsers for the test (Chrome or Safari)
Face covering (online test)
Your face must be fully visible through your webcam during the online test.
We may invite you to take the test in person or with Microsoft Teams if you can’t remove your face covering.
Ceremony accommodations
We may invite you to a virtual or an in-person ceremony.

hits.title: Apply online to visit Canada: IRCC Portal
hits.text:
Updating your information
- How can I change my address or contact information for my immigration or citizenship application?
General technical issues
- What do I do if I have technical problems when applying online?
Web/Internet browsers
- How do I upgrade my web browser?
- Why do I need to clear my browser cache?
Other technical issues
Too many attempts
You may get a failure message if you make too many unsuccessful attempts to sign in during the same session. Close your browser window or tab and try again.
Experiencing technical difficulties
The site could be down for a number of reasons, including for system maintenance. We apologize for the inconvenience. Try again later.
Session expired
For security reasons, your session will be closed if it’s inactive for a certain number of minutes. Sign in again.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Test results and next steps
hits.text:
Print or email your test result as a confirmation
We will not send you a confirmation email after you complete the online test. Also, you can’t sign in to view your results again.
To save a copy of your results for your records, print the test results page, or email the page to yourself using the buttons at the bottom of the page. If you select the “Email” button, we’ll send the results to the email address you provided on your citizenship application form.
If you forgot to save a copy, email the address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation.

hits.title: Citizenship test: If you missed the test
hits.text:
If you missed the test
Find out what to do if you didn’t take the test either during the 30-day period provided in your invitation or when it was scheduled.
You missed your first test the first time we invited you
If this is the first time we invited you, but you missed the test, we’ll automatically send you a new invitation. You still have 3 chances to pass the test within the new 30-day period.
You missed a second test invitation
If this is the second time we invited you, and you didn’t take your test, email the address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation and provide
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
If you missed the test twice and didn’t contact us, we’ll abandon (stop processing) your application. You’ll have to start the application process over if you want to apply for citizenship again.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
If you’re taking the test in person or on Microsoft Teams
If you take the test in person or on Microsoft Teams, your invitation will include the details, for example, the time and location. If you fail the test, you’ll get a new invitation for another time.
How to reschedule the test
If you need to reschedule the test, email the address in the rescheduling section of your test invitation. In your email, include
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule your test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to reschedule your test, but it may take longer.
Urgent processing for emergencies
If you need to take the test before the 30-day period on your invitation due to an emergency, check if you qualify for urgent processing .

hits.title: Apply to renounce (give up) Canadian citizenship urgently
hits.text:
If you have already sent your application and need urgent processing:
Who you should contact depends on where you currently live.
If you live in Canada or the United States
You can use our Web Form or send a letter to the address in the instruction guide .
Use our Web form
Fill out the Web form explaining why you need urgent processing and include:
- your full name, date of birth, email address and telephone numbers
- your unique client identifier (UCI) or application number
- any documents that will support your explanation
- files must in PDF, JPEG, TIFF, DOC, or DOCX format
- files must be 2 MB or smaller

hits.title: Give up (renounce) Canadian citizenship: After you apply
hits.text:
Some applications may take longer to process
- If documents or fees (if applicable) are missing, we will return your application to you.

Check the status of your application online . If the normal processing times have passed and you cannot check the status of your application online, you can send us an enquiry by using this Web form .
A citizenship officer may need to interview you
If so, we’ll notify you by mail of the time and place of your interview.
- If you live outside Canada, the Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate responsible for your area will contact you to let you know how the interview will be conducted.
- If you need to change your appointment, contact the office that sent you the invitation.
- The contact information is in the letter we sent you.
You may withdraw your application . If you do, you may be eligible for a refund .

hits.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements: after you submit your request
hits.text:
If we refuse your waiver request
We’ll send you a letter to let you know if we refuse a request.
You must take the test, prove your language skills or take the oath (depending on the waiver you asked for).
If you need help meeting these requirements, you can request an accommodation for accessibility or another reason .

hits.title: Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
hits.text:
Option 1 (recommended): Reply to your invitation
Reply to the office that sent you the invitation.
Option 2: Send us a web form
You can also request an accommodation by sending us a web form .
If you need a waiver (exemption)
If you have a situation that prevents you from meeting a requirement, you can request a waiver instead of an accommodation. You can request a waiver for these requirements:
- Citizenship test and language requirement: Your situation must meet the waiver criteria .
- Oath of citizenship : We’ll only give a waiver if a mental disability (like an intellectual or a developmental disability) prevents an applicant from understanding the oath.
- For example, they don’t understand that taking the oath makes them a Canadian citizen.
If we approve your waiver request, you don’t need to meet the requirement (for example, you don’t need to take the test).
Learn more about the waiver

hits.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements: after you submit your request
hits.text:
After you submit your waiver request
After we get your request, we’ll
- review it to make sure that you qualify for the waiver
- tell you our decision or ask for more information
We can’t guarantee the approval of a waiver request. Our officers will review all requests on a case-by-case basis.
If we approve your waiver request
You do not need to take the test, prove your language skills or take the oath of citizenship (depending on the waiver of you asked for).
If you check your application status , these sections of the status tracker will have a “ Waived ” status (where applicable):
- Citizenship test
- Language skills
- Citizenship ceremony

hits.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements
hits.text:
Waiver for citizenship requirements
To become a Canadian citizen, you must meet certain requirements when you apply. If you can’t meet a specific requirement, you can request an exemption. This is called a waiver. If your waiver is approved, it means you don’t need to meet that requirement.
You can only request a waiver for
- the citizenship test
- proving your English or French language skills
- the oath of citizenship
If you can meet the requirement but you need help with it , request an accommodation instead .

question: Can I apply for urgent processing of my citizenship application if I need to travel due to a serious illness in my family and cannot get a passport in my current nationality?

hits.title: Apply for citizenship: Urgent processing
hits.text:
Apply for citizenship: Urgent processing
The current processing time for citizenship is We couldn’t load the data. Try again . If your situation is urgent and you need your citizenship sooner, you may apply for urgent processing.
We can only process citizenship applications urgently in exceptional cases , for example if you
- need Canadian citizenship to
- apply for a job
- avoid losing your job
- need to travel because of death or serious illness in your family and you can’t get a passport in your current nationality
- receive a successful Federal Court decision on an appeal on a previous application for citizenship
We check every request to make sure we can process it urgently.
- Even if your application qualifies as an exceptional case, we may not be able to process your request urgently.
- If we process your request urgently, we may not be able to do it in time to help your situation.
- If your application doesn’t qualify as an exceptional case, we’ll process it normally.

hits.title: Apply to resume your citizenship urgently
hits.text:
Apply to resume your citizenship urgently
We can only process requests to resume Canadian citizenship urgently in special cases. Every urgent request will be checked to see if it meets the conditions for urgent processing. If an application does not meet the conditions, it will be processed normally.
To apply for urgent processing, you must meet all the conditions to resume your Canadian citizenship .
Examples of when we may process an application for resumption of citizenship urgently:
- You can't apply for a job or could lose your job because you are not a Canadian citizen.
- You cannot go to a Canadian school, college or university because you are not a Canadian citizen.
- You need to travel because of death or serious illness in the family and cannot get a passport in your current nationality.
- You received a decision on a previous application for citizenship that you successfully appealed to the Federal Court.

hits.title: How to request faster processing of your work permit extension if you need to travel urgently
hits.text:
How to request urgent processing
Request urgent processing using our IRCC web form .
- Select, Update your application (for example, submit documents) .
- Select, Add a document to your application .
- In the “Tell us about your request” section:
- When asked, Did we ask you to add the document(s) to your application? , select, No, I want to add the document(s) to support or complete my application .
- In the textbox, copy and paste the text below and complete the details for your specific situation: Urgent work permit application in Canada – [Travel] or [Death/Serious illness in the family]
- Briefly explain why you need urgent processing.
- Include your travel date.
- State whether or not you can wait 10 business days.
- Keep your explanations brief and factual. Ensure names and dates match your documents .
- Upload your documents.
- Under “Upload your document(s)”, attach the documents you prepared .
Submit an IRCC web form

hits.title: Apply to resume your citizenship urgently
hits.text:
- You received a decision on a previous application for citizenship that you successfully appealed to the Federal Court.
See the Application Processing Times to find out how long it takes to process an application to resume citizenship. If you think you have an emergency and will not be able to resume your citizenship in time, you may apply for urgent processing.
Even if these conditions apply to you, we may not be able to process your request urgently. If we do process your request urgently, we may not be able to do it in time to help your situation.

hits.title: Search of citizenship records: After you apply
hits.text:
If you need urgent processing
We can process applications faster than our normal processing times in special cases , such as
- confirming to a foreign government that you’re not a citizen
- For example, to get a passport from that country.
- showing you are (or are not) a citizen to get a certain job
- administering the estate of a deceased person or executing a will
To ask for urgent processing of your submitted application
- fill out our web form (opens in a new tab) .
- include
- your full name, date of birth, email address and telephone numbers
- a letter explaining why you need urgent processing
- any documents that support your request for urgent processing
- Make sure your document is in the correct format .
We’ll review your request to see if it qualifies. Even if you qualify, we can’t guarantee that you’ll get your search of citizenship record on time.

question: How can I change the email address where I receive my citizenship test link if I haven't received the invitation yet?

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Changing the email that receives the test link
If you want to change your email address before you receive the invitation, use our web form .
If you want to change your email address after you receive the invitation
If you’ve already received your invitation, email the address in your invitation, and include your application number and unique client identifier (UCI).
It will take time for us to update your email. Continue to check your previous email address.
If you have a representative but want the test link sent to your email, follow these instructions:
- Login to the online test.
- Select the “Email me the test link” button, and you’ll see the option to update the email address.
- Select “Yes, I want to use my email address (new email),” and provide the required information.
- You’ll need to know your representative’s email; this should be the email they used to forward your invitation to you.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
If you don’t receive the test link
It may take a few minutes for you or your representative to receive the test link. To see if you received it, check
- for messages from an email address ending in “@cic.gc.ca”
- your email junk or spam folder
If you don’t get the test link and your representative doesn’t either, follow these steps:
- Check your spam or junk folder.
- Add the test link email address to your “safe senders” list: notifications@ct-tc.apps.cic.gc.ca .
- Request the link again by clicking on the “Resend the test link” button.
- Make sure you’re using Chrome or Safari, and turn off any virtual private networks (VPNs).
If you still don’t get the test link, email the address in your test invitation and include
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
How to start the test
- Sign in
- Sign in to the online test only after you receive an invitation.
- Use your application number and your unique client identifier (UCI) to sign in.
- Read and accept the privacy notice, and the terms and conditions.
- Request the test link and check your email
- Select the “Email me the test link” button at the bottom of the page. We’ll send the link to the same email address that received the test invitation (the email on your citizenship application) or your representative’s email.
- If you’re using a representative, you’ll have an option to send the link to your email instead of theirs.
- It may take a few minutes for you or your representative to receive the test link.
- The link expires after 15 minutes. If your link expires, sign in again to get a new test link.
- If you sent yourself a test link multiple times, use the latest test link to sign in.
- Confirm your identity
- Re-enter your application number and UCI to confirm your identity.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
How you’ll get the invitation
If you gave an email address in your application, we’ll send you or your representative the invitation by email .
To avoid missing our emails
- check your junk or spam folder
- look for an invitation from an email address that ends in “@cic.gc.ca” or “@canada.ca”
If you or your representative did not give an email address in your application you can provide your email using our web form . If you don’t provide an email
- we’ll mail the invitation to you or
- we may call you (check your voicemail messages regularly)

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Retaking photos
If your photo is not clear, select the “Retake” button before you approve it.
If you approved the photo , you can still retake it if you haven’t started the test yet. In this case, you must get a new test link by following these steps:
- Wait for at least 15 minutes until your test link expires.
- Sign in again using your application number and unique client identifier (UCI).
- Request a new test link after accepting the terms.
- Retake your photo and take the test.
If you already started the test , you cannot retake your photo.
If you can’t retake your photo, email the address in your test invitation and include
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)

hits.text:
If you haven’t received an invitation by the start date in the status tracker
If your application status says you’ve been scheduled for an online test, but you haven’t received an invitation yet, you should get it soon. They usually arrive at least 2 to 3 business days before your test start date.
If it’s less than 2 to 3 business days before the start date, send an an email to IRCC.CitOnlineTest-TestenligneCit-IRCC@cic.gc.ca with
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)

hits.title: Citizenship test: If you missed the test
hits.text:
You missed your first test
If this was the first time we invited you to the test and you missed it, you have 2 options:
- contact us
- wait for us to reschedule your test
Option 1: Contact us (recommended)
Send an explanation within 30 days of your missed test date to the email address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation. In your email, include
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
You can also send your explanation by mail to the office that scheduled your test if you don’t have an email address. Check your test invitation for the address of that office.
We’ll use the postmark date on your envelope as the date you sent your explanation.
After you contact us, we’ll send you a new invitation.
- If your reason is valid, the new invitation will count as your first invitation.
- If your reason is invalid, the new invitation will count as your final invitation.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Test results and next steps
hits.text:
Print or email your test result as a confirmation
We will not send you a confirmation email after you complete the online test. Also, you can’t sign in to view your results again.
To save a copy of your results for your records, print the test results page, or email the page to yourself using the buttons at the bottom of the page. If you select the “Email” button, we’ll send the results to the email address you provided on your citizenship application form.
If you forgot to save a copy, email the address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
Online test only: If the time between the start and end dates in your invitation is not 30 days
If the time between the start date and the end date of your test is not 30 days, email us
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- a screenshot or attachment of your test invitation
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
Use the email address we provided in your invitation.
When you’ll get a test invitation
Most people get the invitation 1 to 3 months after they receive the acknowledgment of receipt of their application (AOR).
The wait time for an invitation also depends on your situation and our current processing times. For example, you may wait longer if your application is non-routine .
You must wait until you receive your invitation before you can take the test. You can’t book the test yourself or contact us to get an invitation. We’ll send the invitation as quickly as possible.

hits.text:
If you automatically got citizenship when the Citizenship Act changed
There are fewer requirements if you’re giving up your Canadian citizenship because you automatically became a citizen when changes were made to the Citizenship Act . In this situation, you must
- be a citizen of a country other than Canada or become a citizen of a country other than Canada if your application to give up your citizenship is approved
- not be prevented from understanding the significance of giving up your Canadian citizenship because of a mental disability

hits.title: Give up (renounce) Canadian citizenship: How to apply
hits.text:
Submit your application
If you live in Canada or the United States and are applying to:
- renounce under subsection 9(1) of the Citizenship Act , find out where to send your completed application form and the required documents.
- renounce under section 7.1 of the Citizenship Regulations , find out where to send your completed application form and the required documents.
- This is for people who automatically became citizens due to changes to the Citizenship Act.
If you live outside Canada and outside the United States , submit your completed application form and the required documents to the Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate responsible for your area.
Track your application
Track your application
We recommend that you use a postal or courier service that provides a tracking number so you can confirm delivery to IRCC.

Pay your application fees
In most cases, the fee to renounce your citizenship is $100.
There is no fee if you automatically got your citizenship because of changes to the Citizenship Act and are applying under section 7.1 of the Citizenship Regulations.
If you’re submitting more than one application in the same envelope, you can pay all the fees together.
You can pay your fee online (opens in a new tab) . Other ways of paying your fee may be available depending on where you’re applying from.
You can’t get a refund once we start processing your application.

hits.text:

- Download and print the application that applies to you depending on your situation:
- The Application to Renounce Canadian Citizenship is for an adult Canadian citizen who wants to give up citizenship.
- The Application to Renounce Canadian Citizenship – R7.1 should be used if you automatically got citizenship because of changes to the Citizenship Act in 2009 or 2015.
- Complete the application form. Answer all the questions.
- Put the required documents, photograph and fees in the same envelope as the application form. Note: There is no fee for renunciation under R7.1.
- Include an explanation of why you need urgent processing and include any documents that support your explanation.
- Write “Urgent – Renunciation of Canadian Citizenship” in dark letters on the envelope.

If you’re submitting more than one application in the same envelope, you can pay all the fees together.
You can pay your fee online (opens in a new tab) . Other ways of paying your fee may be available depending on where you’re applying from.
You can’t get a refund once we start processing your application.

hits.title: Apply to renounce (give up) Canadian citizenship urgently

- Complete the application form. Answer all the questions.
- Put the required documents, photograph and fees in the same envelope as the application form. Note: There is no fee for renunciation under R7.1.
- Include an explanation of why you need urgent processing and include any documents that support your explanation.
- Write “Urgent – Renunciation of Canadian Citizenship” in dark letters on the envelope.

hits.title: Give up (renounce) Canadian citizenship: How to apply
hits.text:
Give up (renounce) Canadian citizenship: How to apply
- 1. About the process
- 2. Who can apply
- 3. How to apply
- 4. After you apply
Choose an application package
There are 2 application packages available to you. Choose one of the following depending on your situation:
- If you’re a Canadian citizen who wants to give up citizenship , use the Application to Renounce Canadian Citizenship Under Subsection 9(1) .
- If you automatically got citizenship because of changes to the Citizenship Act , use the Application to Renounce Canadian Citizenship – R7.1 .
Read the appropriate guide carefully before you complete the application form. The fee for processing your application is not refundable, so make sure you are eligible to renounce your Canadian citizenship before you apply.
The application kit contains instructions. Read the instructions, and provide the required documents. If information or documents are missing, your application may be delayed.

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for Stateless people: Who can apply
hits.text:
- You were born outside Canada on or after December 15, 2025.
- If you were born before this date but you meet the other requirements, check if you may already be a Canadian citizen .
- You have a parent who was a Canadian citizen when you were born, but you do not meet the requirements for citizenship by descent .
- You have been stateless for your whole life. This means
- you did not automatically become a citizen of any of your parents’ countries of citizenship because of the citizenship laws of those countries
- you did not acquire citizenship from the country you were born in
- you have never applied for and been granted citizenship by any country
- You have been physically present in Canada for at least 1,095 days (3 years) of the 4 years immediately before you apply.
- You’re under 23 years old when you apply.

question: How long do I have to complete the online citizenship test and what happens if I don't finish in time?

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Take the online test
After you receive the invitation, you can take the online citizenship test. Find out what you need to do to prepare for and complete the test.
This page doesn’t apply to the other test formats (in person or on Microsoft Teams).
Getting ready for the test
Citizenship tests are 45 minutes long. Once the timer starts, you won’t be able to stop it. After 45 minutes, your test will be submitted automatically, even if you’re not finished. You’ll get a warning when you have 5 minutes left.
Before you start the test, make sure you’re prepared.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
If needed, we’ll reschedule your test once we’ve reviewed your email. It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to reschedule your test, but it may take longer.
For your rescheduled test, you may have to
- do an interview with our officer or
- retake the test by video conference, if necessary

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
If you’re disconnected during the test or can’t finish it due to technical issues
If you’re disconnected during the online test, use the most recent test link we sent you to return to the test as soon as possible. You may have to sign in again and request a new link if the test link expired.
The 45-minute timer continues while you’re disconnected. If you go past the 45-minute time limit while disconnected, our system will automatically submit your test and all the answers you selected up to that point.
You won’t see your test result when you sign in. To get your result, email the address in your test invitation and include
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
You have 30 days from the start date in your invitation to contact us.
If needed, we’ll reschedule your test once we’ve reviewed your email. It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to reschedule your test, but it may take longer.
For your rescheduled test, you may have to

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
When you can take the test
If you take the test online , you can take your test only between the start date and end date provided on your invitation. This will be a 30-day period.
After you receive your invitation, you
- have up to 3 chances to pass the test during the 30-day period
- If you fail, log in and try again to use your chances.
- can take the test at any time during the 30-day period (including weekends and holidays)
You can’t sign in to the test
- before or after the 30-day period on your invitation or
- after you submit the test

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:

- If you can’t return to the test within 45 minutes, email the address in your test invitation and include
- a detailed explanation of the issue and how you tried to fix it

We’ll reschedule your test once we’ve reviewed your email. It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to reschedule your test, but it may take longer.

hits.title: Citizenship test: If you missed the test
hits.text:
If you missed the test
Find out what to do if you didn’t take the test either during the 30-day period provided in your invitation or when it was scheduled.
You missed your first test the first time we invited you
If this is the first time we invited you, but you missed the test, we’ll automatically send you a new invitation. You still have 3 chances to pass the test within the new 30-day period.
You missed a second test invitation
If this is the second time we invited you, and you didn’t take your test, email the address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation and provide
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
If you missed the test twice and didn’t contact us, we’ll abandon (stop processing) your application. You’ll have to start the application process over if you want to apply for citizenship again.
