hits.title: Final instructions to apply for an eTA
hits.text:
If you had an eTA that was cancelled, make sure you’re still eligible before you apply
As of February 29, 2024, you need to meet all 3 of these requirements to be eligible for an eTA:
- You’re using a valid Mexican passport to fly to Canada or to transit through a Canadian airport to another destination.
- You’re coming to Canada for a short visit (normally for stays of up to 6 months).
- You either
- currently hold a valid United States (US) non-immigrant visa , or
- have held a Canadian visitor visa (a temporary resident visa) in the past 10 years
- A visitor visa is not the same as an eTA.
- Having held an eTA in the past 10 years is not the same as having held a Canadian visitor visa.
- If you held a Canadian visitor visa in the last 10 years, the counterfoil would have been affixed to your passport.
If you don’t meet the above requirements, you need to apply for a visitor visa .
Find out more:

hits.title: Transit through Canada
hits.text:
eTA
You need an eTA to transit through Canada by air if you’re from an eTA-required country .
You don’t need an eTA if you’re transiting through Canada and you enter by train, bus, boat or cruise ship. You do need to bring the right travel documents .
Apply for an eTA
Citizens and permanent residents of the United States
US citizens and lawful permanent residents of the U.S. can transit through Canada without a visa by:
- air
- car
- bus
- train
- boat
- cruise ship
You just need to bring the right travel documents .

hits.title: Super visa for parents and grandparents: Who can apply
hits.text:
General requirements for visiting Canada
There are some general conditions you must meet to come to Canada as a visitor. Before we make a decision on your application, we’ll also consider
- whether you’re a genuine visitor to Canada who will leave by choice at the end of your visit
- your ties to your home country
- the purpose of your visit
- your family and finances
Visa-exempt applicants
Even if you don’t need a visitor visa to enter Canada, you can still get a super visa to stay in Canada for 5 years. If we approve your application, we’ll issue you a letter to give to a border services officer when you arrive in Canada.
If you travel by air , you may also need to apply for an electronic travel authorization (eTA) separately to allow you to travel to and enter Canada. The eTA will be electronically linked to your passport, so you need to travel with the passport you used to apply for your eTA and any supporting documents for your super visa application.

Application process for airport authorities and air carriers: Transit Without Visa Program and China Transit Program
Airport authorities and air carriers that meet the minimum Transit Without Visa (TWOV) Program and/or China Transit Program (CTP) eligibility criteria can apply for the program.
All airport authorities and air carriers must submit 2 copies of their application form: one for Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) and another one for the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
Completed application forms will be jointly assessed by IRCC and the CBSA. If you don’t complete the required fields in the application form, there will be a delay in the assessment process.
If the application is approved, applicants must sign a TWOV Program or CTP memorandum of understanding (MOU) with IRCC and the CBSA to ensure their eligibility.

question: Can I sponsor my step-parent as the principal applicant on the same application as my biological parent?

hits.title: Sponsor your parents and grandparents: Who you can sponsor
hits.text:
Sponsoring your biological or adopted parent, your step-parent and their child
You can sponsor your parent, their spouse and their child (your half-sibling). On the application, your parent must be the principal applicant, because they’re related to you. Your step-parent can’t be the principal applicant. They’ll be listed as your parent’s dependant. Your half-sibling can be added as a dependant only if they qualify as a dependent child .
Sponsoring your grandparents, your parent and your step-parent
In this situation, you’ll have to submit 2 separate sponsorship applications: 1 application per couple.
On your grandparents’ application, you must designate one of them as the principal applicant. You’ll designate their spouse (your other grandparent) as a dependant.

hits.title: Sponsor your parents and grandparents: Who you can sponsor
hits.text:
On your grandparents’ application, you must designate one of them as the principal applicant. You’ll designate their spouse (your other grandparent) as a dependant.
It’s important to make sure that you have designated the appropriate grandparent as the principal applicant because once you’ve submitted your application, you can’t change the grandparent you designated as the principal applicant.
On your parent’s application, they must be the principal applicant, because they’re related to you. Their spouse can’t be the principal applicant. They’ll be listed as your parent’s dependant.

hits.title: Sponsor your parents and grandparents: Who you can sponsor
hits.text:
Sponsoring your biological or adopted parents, together as a couple
You can sponsor your parents together if they’re a couple (married or in a common-law relationship). On the application, you must designate 1 of them as the main applicant, called the principal applicant. You’ll designate their spouse (your other parent) as a dependant.
It’s important to make sure that you have designated the appropriate parent or grandparent as the principal applicant because once you’ve submitted your application, you can’t change the parent you designated as the principal applicant.
If you have siblings, you can include them in the application only if they qualify as dependent children . If they’re older than the age limit or they don’t meet all the requirements, you can’t include them in your parents’ or grandparents’ application. They’ll have to immigrate on their own if they want to live in Canada.

hits.text:
After they get this letter, the principal applicant can link their application to their online account. This way, they can communicate with us quickly and securely and get updates and messages about their application online.
Find out how to create an online account and link an application .
You (the sponsor) can link their application for them if you’re managing your family members’ application and you’re designated as their representative.

hits.title: What it means to be a sponsor
hits.text:
What it means to be a sponsor
Being a sponsor means you commit to support the people you’re sponsoring (your parents and grandparents and their accompanying family members, if applicable) for a period of time, even if your situation changes.
To become a sponsor, you must sign an undertaking and a sponsorship agreement.
The undertaking
To become a sponsor, you must sign an undertaking . In the undertaking, you’ll commit to
- financially supporting the people you’re sponsoring for a period of time, called the undertaking period
- The undertaking period to sponsor your parents and grandparents is 20 years. If you live in Quebec, it’s 10 years.
- The undertaking period starts the day the people you’re sponsoring become permanent residents.
- making sure the people you’re sponsoring won’t need to ask the government for social assistance

question: How long am I responsible for financially supporting my sponsored relative and their family members under the relative sponsorship program?

hits.title: Sponsor your relatives: Check if you’re eligible
hits.text:
Your responsibilities
When you sponsor a relative to become a permanent resident of Canada, you must commit to
- financially supporting them and their accompanying family members
- beginning on the date they become a permanent resident
- for up to 20 years (depending on their age and how you’re related)
- making sure they won’t need to ask the government for social assistance
- If they receive social assistance during the time you’re responsible for them, you’ll have to re-pay the amount. You won’t be able to sponsor anyone else until you’ve re-paid it.
The person you sponsor must sign an agreement saying they will make the effort to support themselves and their accompanying family members. This includes sponsored dependent children 22 years or older. Dependent children under 22 don’t have to sign this agreement.

question: Can I change the principal applicant after submitting the application for the Parents and Grandparents Program?

hits.title: Sponsor your parents and grandparents: Who you can sponsor
hits.text:
On your grandparents’ application, you must designate one of them as the principal applicant. You’ll designate their spouse (your other grandparent) as a dependant.
It’s important to make sure that you have designated the appropriate grandparent as the principal applicant because once you’ve submitted your application, you can’t change the grandparent you designated as the principal applicant.
On your parent’s application, they must be the principal applicant, because they’re related to you. Their spouse can’t be the principal applicant. They’ll be listed as your parent’s dependant.

hits.title: Sponsor your parents and grandparents: Who you can sponsor
hits.text:
Sponsoring your biological or adopted parents, together as a couple
You can sponsor your parents together if they’re a couple (married or in a common-law relationship). On the application, you must designate 1 of them as the main applicant, called the principal applicant. You’ll designate their spouse (your other parent) as a dependant.
It’s important to make sure that you have designated the appropriate parent or grandparent as the principal applicant because once you’ve submitted your application, you can’t change the parent you designated as the principal applicant.
If you have siblings, you can include them in the application only if they qualify as dependent children . If they’re older than the age limit or they don’t meet all the requirements, you can’t include them in your parents’ or grandparents’ application. They’ll have to immigrate on their own if they want to live in Canada.

Check if you’re eligible
If you’re eligible, you can sponsor your parents and grandparents, related by blood or adoption.
Who can sponsor their parents and grandparents
You can sponsor your biological or adopted parents and grandparents if

- you’re at least 18 years old
- you live in Canada
- Your primary residential address must be in Canada when you submit your application and until we make a decision on your application.

- you have enough money to support the people you want to sponsor

- you may have a spouse or common-law partner co-sign the application to combine your incomes

- On the form Financial Evaluation for Parents and Grandparents Sponsorship [IMM 5768] (PDF, 171 KB) , under question 8, “Sponsor Statement of Consent”:

hits.text:

Authorized paid representatives (APRs) can submit your work permit application on your behalf through the APR Portal .

hits.text:

The AOR letter means that an officer has reviewed your application package and confirmed that it’s complete .

question: Can I sponsor my relatives if I am a permanent resident of Canada and at least 18 years old?

hits.title: Sponsor your relatives: Check if you’re eligible
hits.text:
Who can sponsor
You can sponsor certain relatives if you
- are at least 18 years old
- are a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident of Canada, or a person registered in Canada under the Canadian Indian Act
- live in Canada
- Your primary residential address must be in Canada when you submit your application and until we make a decision on your application.
- meet set income guidelines
If you live in Quebec
You must meet Quebec’s eligibility requirements for sponsoring another relative .
You must also complete an undertaking with the Government of Quebec.
Don’t submit your undertaking application to Quebec until we tell you to do so . If you don’t wait for our confirmation, Quebec won’t process your application .

hits.title: Sponsor your relatives: How to apply
hits.text:
How to apply
There are two stages in the process for your eligible relatives to become permanent residents.
- You apply to sponsor your relatives.
- Your family members must apply for permanent residence.
You must send both your sponsorship application and the permanent residence application for your relatives at the same time .
To apply as a sponsor, you must be at least 18 years of age and a:
- Canadian citizen or
- person registered in Canada as an Indian under the Canadian Indian Act or
- permanent resident of Canada
We’ll process your application to sponsor and write you to tell you if we approve your application.

hits.title: Sponsor your spouse, partner or children: Who you can sponsor
hits.text:
Who you can sponsor
Your spouse, common-law partner, conjugal partner and dependent child must meet certain requirements to become permanent residents of Canada.
Sponsor your spouse
Your spouse
- is legally married to you
- is at least 18 years old
- can be any gender
- is in a genuine relationship with you, not only for the purpose of getting permanent resident status
- must not be inadmissible to Canada
Sponsor your common-law partner
Your common-law partner
- is not legally married to you
- is at least 18 years old
- can be any gender
- is in a genuine relationship with you, not only for the purpose of getting permanent resident status
- has lived with you for at least 12 consecutive months, meaning
- you’ve lived together continuously for 1 year in a conjugal relationship, without any long periods apart
- any time spent away from each other during the 12-month period should have been short and temporary (for example, for family obligations or business travel)

hits.title: Sponsor your relatives: Check if you’re eligible
hits.text:
Your responsibilities
When you sponsor a relative to become a permanent resident of Canada, you must commit to
- financially supporting them and their accompanying family members
- beginning on the date they become a permanent resident
- for up to 20 years (depending on their age and how you’re related)
- making sure they won’t need to ask the government for social assistance
- If they receive social assistance during the time you’re responsible for them, you’ll have to re-pay the amount. You won’t be able to sponsor anyone else until you’ve re-paid it.
The person you sponsor must sign an agreement saying they will make the effort to support themselves and their accompanying family members. This includes sponsored dependent children 22 years or older. Dependent children under 22 don’t have to sign this agreement.

- you meet all other requirements under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations

question: Can someone else sign my application form for the spouse or partner sponsorship program electronically on my behalf?

hits.text:
- answer questions about the forms
They can’t:

- electronically sign the application for you
- sign in to the portal using your username and password
After you read the declaration, you must be the one to type your name. This is the legal requirement for your application to be considered “signed” according to Canada’s immigration law.
You don’t need to hire a representative. Using one will not draw special attention to your application and doesn’t mean we’ll approve it.

hits.text:
If you’re getting help with your application from someone else
You can ask someone to help you with your application.
There are special requirements depending on what kind of help you’re getting:
If you’re using a paid immigration representative
Paid representatives need to be authorized (opens in a new tab) .
If you want to use a paid representative, you must:
- download the Use of a Representative (IMM 5476) form
- complete and sign it
- get your representative to sign it
- upload it with your application
A paid representative can fill out forms and communicate with us for you through their own account. They can also:
- help you prepare the documents you need to upload
- answer questions about the forms
They can’t:
- open a portal account on your behalf
- electronically sign the application for you
- sign in to the portal using your username and password

hits.text:
If you’re using an unpaid representative
Unpaid representatives don’t need to be authorized or certified. They can be:
- family members
- friends
- anyone else who doesn’t charge you a fee
If you want to use an unpaid representative, you must:
- submit the Use of a Representative (IMM 5476 ) form
- complete and sign it
- get your representative to sign it
- upload it with your application
An unpaid representative can:
- help you open a portal account
- fill out forms for you, but not sign them
- communicate with us for you
- help you prepare the documents you need to upload
- answer questions about forms

hits.title: Income requirements for the sponsor

To prove you meet the income requirements, you must provide a notice of assessment from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for each of the 3 tax years before the date you apply.

- Give us permission to get your tax information directly from CRA
- On the form Financial Evaluation for Parents and Grandparents Sponsorship [IMM 5768] (PDF, 171 KB) , under question 8, “Sponsor Statement of Consent”:
- Check “Yes.”
- Provide your social insurance number (SIN), signature and date.
- Send us the paper copies of your notices of assessment
- Complete the form Income Sources for the Sponsorship of Parents and Grandparents [IMM 5748] (PDF, 154 KB) .
- Include the notices of assessment with your application package. If you don’t have the paper copies, log in to CRA’s My Account to find them online.

question: Can I apply for Canadian citizenship as a stateless person if I was born outside Canada before December 15, 2025?

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for Stateless people: Who can apply
hits.text:
Who can apply
This page explains who is eligible to apply for Canadian citizenship as a stateless person, what it means to be a stateless person and who should fill out the forms.
If you applied as a stateless person before December 15, 2025
On December 15, 2025, the Government of Canada passed Bill C-3 to change the first-­generation limit on citizenship by descent. If you meet the new requirements for citizenship by descent, we’ll contact you for next steps.
Learn more about this change .
This application is only for stateless people who meet certain conditions. A person is stateless if no country or state recognizes them as a citizen or national.
To be eligible for this application, you must be a stateless person and meet all of these other conditions:
- You were born outside Canada on or after December 15, 2025.
- If you were born before this date but you meet the other requirements, check if you may already be a Canadian citizen .

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for Stateless people: Who can apply
hits.text:
- You were born outside Canada on or after December 15, 2025.
- If you were born before this date but you meet the other requirements, check if you may already be a Canadian citizen .
- You have a parent who was a Canadian citizen when you were born, but you do not meet the requirements for citizenship by descent .
- You have been stateless for your whole life. This means
- you did not automatically become a citizen of any of your parents’ countries of citizenship because of the citizenship laws of those countries
- you did not acquire citizenship from the country you were born in
- you have never applied for and been granted citizenship by any country
- You have been physically present in Canada for at least 1,095 days (3 years) of the 4 years immediately before you apply.
- You’re under 23 years old when you apply.
Even if you meet the requirements above, you may not be eligible for a grant of citizenship if you were one of the following:

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
hits.text:
If you were born in Canada
A provincial or territorial birth certificate should be enough to prove Canadian citizenship.
You may still apply for a citizenship certificate .
If you were born outside Canada to a Canadian parent
You may be a Canadian citizen if your parent was a Canadian citizen when you were born. Some limits apply.
Check if you may be a Canadian citizen. If you want to find out for sure , apply for a citizenship certificate.
If you were born outside Canada on or after December 15, 2025 , and your Canadian parent was born outside Canada, you must prove that your Canadian parent spent 1,095 days in Canada before you were born.
Calculate your parent’s physical presence .

hits.text:
Exceptions for some citizenship applications
If you apply as a stateless person born to a Canadian parent , the certificate is available in paper format only at this time.
We’re working to make sure the e-certificate is available to all successful citizenship applicants in the future.

Canadian citizenship
Apply to become a Canadian citizen, study for the test or get proof of citizenship.
Status of changes to the first-generation limit on citizenship by descent Updated December 15, 2025
On December 15, 2025, the Government of Canada passed Bill C-3 to change the first-generation limit on citizenship by descent.

question: What documents can I provide to prove my physical presence in Canada for stateless person citizenship application?

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for Stateless people: Get the forms and documents
hits.text:
Gather the required documents
These documents are required for all applications:
- a copy of your birth certificate
- personal identification documents (1 regular, 1 with photo)
- two citizenship photos
- proof of a parent’s Canadian citizenship at your birth
- proof that you have always been stateless

A copy of your birth certificate Always required
We’ll use a copy of your birth certificate to prove your date of birth, place of birth and parentage.
Personal identification documents (1 regular, 1 with photo) Always required
Provide copies of 2 types of personal identification (ID) documents.
- Prepare 1 copy per document.
- If there’s information on the front and back of the document, copy both sides.
Each ID document must have your
- name
- date of birth
One of your ID document must also show your photo.

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for Stateless people: Get the forms and documents
hits.text:
Proof of your physical presence in Canada Always required
You must have been physically present in Canada for at least 1,095 days (3 years) in the 4 years immediately before you apply. Gather documents to show your physical presence, such as
- entry or immigration documents (for example, a temporary resident permit or immigration visa)
- travel documents from the Red Cross or International Organization for Migration
- a Canada Revenue Agency notice of assessment
- school records (for example, transcripts or letters confirming attendance)
- health records with dates of care received in Canada
- immunization records for your children
- Gather the supporting documents you might need

- birth certificate

Proof that you have always been stateless Always required
You must provide documents that show you’ve never held any citizenship or nationality. These can include
- a letter from the country or territory where you were born and where you lived stating that you have never been a citizen or national there
- a letter or similar document from every country or territory of your parents’ citizenship or nationality (other than Canadian) confirming that you didn’t gain citizenship or nationality through them

hits.title: Canadian citizenship for stateless people: Submit your application
hits.text:
Mail your application
To avoid delays or a return of your application package, follow these steps before you mail it.
- Before you sign the form
- Confirm you still meet the citizenship eligibility requirements.
- Check completeness
- Confirm that you have included every required form, document and payment receipt.
- If applying as a family or a group, put all complete applications and receipts in one envelope so that we can process them together.
- If any application is incomplete, we will return the entire package
- Sign and date the form
- Sign the application form yourself.
- Use the actual date you sign the form. Do not back-date or post-date.
- The date you sign your application form must be the date you enter in the physical presence calculation section (section 9, line B).
- Send the package right away
- Courier or mail the application package within 90 days of the signature date.

Citizenship certificates
A citizenship certificate is an official document that proves your Canadian citizenship. You’ll get the certificate after we approve your application

Start your affidavit with the following statement:
[Your name] of the [city or town] in the [province or territory] affirm that

After we get your request, we’ll

We can’t guarantee the approval of a waiver request. Our officers will review all requests on a case-by-case basis.

hits.title: Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
hits.text:
Option 1 (recommended): Reply to your invitation
Reply to the office that sent you the invitation.
Option 2: Send us a web form
You can also request an accommodation by sending us a web form .
If you need a waiver (exemption)
If you have a situation that prevents you from meeting a requirement, you can request a waiver instead of an accommodation. You can request a waiver for these requirements:
- Citizenship test and language requirement: Your situation must meet the waiver criteria .
- Oath of citizenship : We’ll only give a waiver if a mental disability (like an intellectual or a developmental disability) prevents an applicant from understanding the oath.
- For example, they don’t understand that taking the oath makes them a Canadian citizen.
If we approve your waiver request, you don’t need to meet the requirement (for example, you don’t need to take the test).
Learn more about the waiver

hits.title: Waiver for citizenship requirements
hits.text:
Waiver for citizenship requirements
To become a Canadian citizen, you must meet certain requirements when you apply. If you can’t meet a specific requirement, you can request an exemption. This is called a waiver. If your waiver is approved, it means you don’t need to meet that requirement.
You can only request a waiver for
- the citizenship test
- proving your English or French language skills
- the oath of citizenship
If you can meet the requirement but you need help with it , request an accommodation instead .

question: What should I do if the time between the start and end dates in my citizenship test invitation is not 30 days?

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
Online test only: If the time between the start and end dates in your invitation is not 30 days
If the time between the start date and the end date of your test is not 30 days, email us
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- a screenshot or attachment of your test invitation
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
Use the email address we provided in your invitation.
When you’ll get a test invitation
Most people get the invitation 1 to 3 months after they receive the acknowledgment of receipt of their application (AOR).
The wait time for an invitation also depends on your situation and our current processing times. For example, you may wait longer if your application is non-routine .
You must wait until you receive your invitation before you can take the test. You can’t book the test yourself or contact us to get an invitation. We’ll send the invitation as quickly as possible.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
You must wait until you receive your invitation before you can take the test. You can’t book the test yourself or contact us to get an invitation. We’ll send the invitation as quickly as possible.
You can check your application status to confirm that your invitation is on its way. When you check, go to the “Citizenship test” section of the status tracker. The In progress status means that
- we have scheduled your test
- you’ll get your invitation soon
Check your application status

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
When you can take the test
If you take the test online , you can take your test only between the start date and end date provided on your invitation. This will be a 30-day period.
After you receive your invitation, you
- have up to 3 chances to pass the test during the 30-day period
- If you fail, log in and try again to use your chances.
- can take the test at any time during the 30-day period (including weekends and holidays)
You can’t sign in to the test
- before or after the 30-day period on your invitation or
- after you submit the test

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
Wait for a test invitation
You need an invitation to take the test online.
What’s on the invitation
We’ll send you an invitation by email to take the online test after you submit your citizenship application. The test invitation is a PDF attachment in an email. The PDF includes instructions on what to do before, during and after the test.
Your invitation should have
- a test start date and end date (you’ll have 30 days to take it)
- a link to the test (or directions for an in-person test)
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
- an email address you can use to contact us

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
If you haven’t received an invitation by the start date in the status tracker
If your application status says you’ve been scheduled for an online test, but you haven’t received an invitation yet, you should get it soon. They usually arrive at least 2 to 3 business days before your test start date.
If it’s less than 2 to 3 business days before the start date, send an an email to IRCC.CitOnlineTest-TestenligneCit-IRCC@cic.gc.ca with
- a detailed explanation of the issue

hits.title: Citizenship test: If you missed the test
hits.text:
If you missed the test
Find out what to do if you didn’t take the test either during the 30-day period provided in your invitation or when it was scheduled.
You missed your first test the first time we invited you
If this is the first time we invited you, but you missed the test, we’ll automatically send you a new invitation. You still have 3 chances to pass the test within the new 30-day period.
You missed a second test invitation
If this is the second time we invited you, and you didn’t take your test, email the address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation and provide
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
If you missed the test twice and didn’t contact us, we’ll abandon (stop processing) your application. You’ll have to start the application process over if you want to apply for citizenship again.

hits.title: Citizenship test: If you missed the test
hits.text:
You missed your first test
If this was the first time we invited you to the test and you missed it, you have 2 options:
- contact us
- wait for us to reschedule your test
Option 1: Contact us (recommended)
Send an explanation within 30 days of your missed test date to the email address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation. In your email, include
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
You can also send your explanation by mail to the office that scheduled your test if you don’t have an email address. Check your test invitation for the address of that office.
We’ll use the postmark date on your envelope as the date you sent your explanation.
After you contact us, we’ll send you a new invitation.
- If your reason is valid, the new invitation will count as your first invitation.
- If your reason is invalid, the new invitation will count as your final invitation.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Take the online test
After you receive the invitation, you can take the online citizenship test. Find out what you need to do to prepare for and complete the test.
This page doesn’t apply to the other test formats (in person or on Microsoft Teams).
Getting ready for the test
Citizenship tests are 45 minutes long. Once the timer starts, you won’t be able to stop it. After 45 minutes, your test will be submitted automatically, even if you’re not finished. You’ll get a warning when you have 5 minutes left.
Before you start the test, make sure you’re prepared.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
If you’re disconnected during the test or can’t finish it due to technical issues
If you’re disconnected during the online test, use the most recent test link we sent you to return to the test as soon as possible. You may have to sign in again and request a new link if the test link expired.
The 45-minute timer continues while you’re disconnected. If you go past the 45-minute time limit while disconnected, our system will automatically submit your test and all the answers you selected up to that point.
You won’t see your test result when you sign in. To get your result, email the address in your test invitation and include
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
You have 30 days from the start date in your invitation to contact us.
If needed, we’ll reschedule your test once we’ve reviewed your email. It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to reschedule your test, but it may take longer.
For your rescheduled test, you may have to

hits.title: Citizenship test: Test results and next steps
hits.text:
Official test result
For tests taken in person and on Microsoft Teams , you’ll get your official test score right after you take the test.
After you take the online test , one of our officers will review your result to make it official. This could take a few days or a few weeks. There are 3 possible test results:
Pass
You correctly answered at least 15 of the 20 questions (75%).
Fail
You failed all your test attempts during the 30-day period in your invitation.
Invalidated
Your test result may be invalid if
- we find out or suspect that you cheated
- a technical issue prevents us from confirming your identity or your test score

question: Can my 14-year-old child use a Canadian citizenship card to travel between Canada and the United States by land or sea without a passport?

hits.title: Valid proofs of Canadian citizenship
hits.text:
If you’re travelling abroad or returning to Canada
Proof of citizenship is not a passport or travel document.
- For example, a border agent at an airport won’t accept a citizenship certificate or card as a passport replacement.
- To travel abroad and return to Canada, you must have a valid passport or travel document (opens in a new tab) .
Exception: Children 15 and under who travel between United States and Canada by land or sea
If there’s no passport, they can use
- a Canadian citizenship card
- an original or a copy of their Canadian birth certificate
- It should be issued by the province or territory where they were born.
- an original Canadian citizenship certificate
When they turn 16, they will need a passport to enter the US.
Learn more about travelling to the US from Canada (opens in a new tab) .

A citizenship certificate is a document that proves your Canadian citizenship.
- You can use it to access various services and benefits, such as a pension, or apply for a passport.
- The certificate is not a travel document.
- If you’re travelling abroad, you must have a valid passport or travel document .
Exception: Children 15 and under don’t need a passport to enter the United States or return to Canada by land or sea.
Documents children 15 and under can use instead of a passport:
- original or copy of their birth certificate
- It should be issued by the vital statistics department from the province or territory where they were born.
- original Canadian citizenship certificate
- Canadian citizenship card
When they turn 16, they need a passport if they’re going to enter the US.
Learn more about travelling to the US from Canada .

hits.title: Dual Canadian citizens need a valid Canadian passport
hits.text:
Canadian-American dual citizens
To fly to Canada, you need
- either your valid U.S. passport or your valid Canadian passport
- to meet the basic requirements to enter Canada
If you travel with just your valid U.S. passport, you
- will need to carry identification that shows your Canadian citizenship
- may be asked to go through immigration screening
Even though you only need one of your passports to enter Canada, you should travel with both . Having both passports makes travel between Canada and the United States easier. Your passports prove
- your citizenships
- that you have the right to enter Canada and the U.S. without immigration screening

When they turn 16, they need a passport if they’re going to enter the US.

hits.title: Minor children travelling to Canada
hits.text:
Minor children entering Canada as a visitor
The documents a minor child needs to enter Canada depend on whether the child is travelling alone or with someone.
If a minor child is travelling alone
The child should present
- their own passport
- A parent’s passport, even if the child’s details are included in it, cannot be used.
- a copy of their birth certificate, and
- a letter of authorization, in English or French if possible, which is signed by both parents or by their legal guardian and includes
- the parents’ (or legal guardian’s) address and telephone number, and
- the name, address and telephone number of the adult who will look after the child in Canada

question: What happens after I submit my application to resume Canadian citizenship?

hits.title: Resume Canadian citizenship: After you apply
hits.text:
Once your application is received at the Case Processing Centre in Sydney, Nova Scotia, it will be reviewed and we will start processing it.
Some applications may encounter delays. For example, if documents are missing or if your case is complex, we may contact you to get more information or to ask you to send us additional information. Such cases may take longer to process.
To find out how long it takes to process applications to resume your Canadian citizenship, see processing times . You can check the status of your application on line .
If you cannot see the status of your application online, and the normal processing times have passed, you may contact us by using this Web form .

question: Can I retake my photo for the citizenship test if I have already started the test?

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Retaking photos
If your photo is not clear, select the “Retake” button before you approve it.
If you approved the photo , you can still retake it if you haven’t started the test yet. In this case, you must get a new test link by following these steps:
- Wait for at least 15 minutes until your test link expires.
- Sign in again using your application number and unique client identifier (UCI).
- Request a new test link after accepting the terms.
- Retake your photo and take the test.
If you already started the test , you cannot retake your photo.
If you can’t retake your photo, email the address in your test invitation and include
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
What to do and not to do during the test
To avoid having to retake the test for a technical reason, make sure you
- turn on your webcam and check that your face is fully visible in the frame
- have a reliable Internet connection
- have no other tabs, windows or programs open on the computer
- turn off your virtual private network (VPN)
- give yourself enough time to take the test (because the timer can’t be paused)
For your test to be valid, you must
- take the test alone
- take the test in the same place you took the photo of yourself and your ID before the test
- make sure there are no items in the background that have your personal information on them (like a diploma)
There are also some things you must not do during the test:
- Don’t use any other devices.
- Don’t look at any study materials.
- Don’t use the back button in your web browser.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
- If you sent yourself a test link multiple times, use the latest test link to sign in.
- Confirm your identity
- Re-enter your application number and UCI to confirm your identity.
- Take photos of your identification (ID) and yourself
- Your ID can be your permanent resident (PR) card or a valid piece of ID with your photo and signature on it (for example, a driver’s licence or health card).
- Wear appropriate clothing for your photo. You may wear traditional or religious clothing, head coverings, and reading or prescription glasses, but your face must be clearly visible.
- If your photos look blurred, your test may be invalid, and we may ask you to take the test again.
- Start the test
- When you’re ready to start the test, select the “Start the test” button. The 45-minute countdown will begin.
Go to the test

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Taking clear photos
Your photos must be clear and easy to see. Make sure that the information on your ID is easy to read.
If either the photo of your personal ID or of your face is unclear
- move your ID closer to the webcam
- change your webcam setting or brightness
- adjust the lighting of you test location or
- use a different device
If we can’t clearly see your photos, your test result may be invalid, and you may have to take the test again.
Accidentally taking a photo of your face instead of your identification (ID)
If you accidentally took a picture of your face instead of your photo ID, you don’t have to contact us. We’ll review your test result and contact you with your next steps.
Depending on the result of our review, your test result may be invalid, and we may send you a new invitation. If you have to take the test again, it can take a few weeks or months to schedule it.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Black or static image on webcam during the test
If your webcam shows a black or static image during the test, follow these steps:
- Try using a different device to take the test.
- If you can’t return to the test within 45 minutes, email the address in your test invitation and include
- a detailed explanation of the issue and how you tried to fix it
- whether you have a different device to take the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
We’ll reschedule your test once we’ve reviewed your email. It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to reschedule your test, but it may take longer.

Option 2: Wait for us to reschedule you
We’ll automatically reschedule your first test if
- you didn’t contact us to explain why you missed it previously, or
- you contact us, but your reason for missing the test is invalid
We’ll send you a final invitation with the rescheduled date (usually 2 weeks after the date of your missed test).
We may stop processing your application if you miss it again.
You missed your second test
If you missed your test, you need to contact us (option 1).
If you contact us and give a valid reason for missing the test, we’ll send you a final invitation. We may stop processing your application if you miss it again.
If we stop processing your application and you still want to become a Canadian citizen, you must reapply and pay the fees again.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
When you can take the test
If you take the test online , you can take your test only between the start date and end date provided on your invitation. This will be a 30-day period.
After you receive your invitation, you
- have up to 3 chances to pass the test during the 30-day period
- If you fail, log in and try again to use your chances.
- can take the test at any time during the 30-day period (including weekends and holidays)
You can’t sign in to the test
- before or after the 30-day period on your invitation or
- after you submit the test

hits.title: Citizenship test: If you missed the test
hits.text:
If you missed the test
Find out what to do if you didn’t take the test either during the 30-day period provided in your invitation or when it was scheduled.
You missed your first test the first time we invited you
If this is the first time we invited you, but you missed the test, we’ll automatically send you a new invitation. You still have 3 chances to pass the test within the new 30-day period.
You missed a second test invitation
If this is the second time we invited you, and you didn’t take your test, email the address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation and provide
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
If you missed the test twice and didn’t contact us, we’ll abandon (stop processing) your application. You’ll have to start the application process over if you want to apply for citizenship again.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Test results and next steps
hits.text:
What to expect if you’re invited to an interview
We may invite you to an interview to
- verify your identity
- authenticate photocopies of your documents
- verify if you’re eligible for Canadian citizenship
Interviews will not necessarily result in a final decision.
When you come for your interview, bring
- the original documents you sent with your application
- any passport or travel documents you used in the 5 years before you applied
If you fail the test
Within your 30-day test period, you have up to 3 chances to pass the test (whether online, on Microsoft Teams, or in person).
If you fail the test all 3 times, we’ll invite you to a hearing with a citizenship official.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Test results and next steps
hits.text:
Print or email your test result as a confirmation
We will not send you a confirmation email after you complete the online test. Also, you can’t sign in to view your results again.
To save a copy of your results for your records, print the test results page, or email the page to yourself using the buttons at the bottom of the page. If you select the “Email” button, we’ll send the results to the email address you provided on your citizenship application form.
If you forgot to save a copy, email the address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation.

question: Can I apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate if I was born in Canada and have a provincial or territorial birth certificate?

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
hits.text:
If you were born in Canada
A provincial or territorial birth certificate should be enough to prove Canadian citizenship.
You may still apply for a citizenship certificate .
If you were born outside Canada to a Canadian parent
You may be a Canadian citizen if your parent was a Canadian citizen when you were born. Some limits apply.
Check if you may be a Canadian citizen. If you want to find out for sure , apply for a citizenship certificate.
If you were born outside Canada on or after December 15, 2025 , and your Canadian parent was born outside Canada, you must prove that your Canadian parent spent 1,095 days in Canada before you were born.
Calculate your parent’s physical presence .

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
hits.text:
What we accept
You must include proof of parentage and Canadian citizenship for your Canadian parent, grandparent and parental ancestor as applicable. For each person, you must provide 1 or more of the following documents issued by the original authority:
provincial or territorial birth certificate
If you’re missing any birth certificates
If you don’t have a birth certificate or birth record for yourself or for any of your parental ancestors, you must send other documents to show parentage and Canadian citizenship. These must be issued by the original authority and can include:
- hospital record of birth
- record from a physician or midwife who witnessed the birth
- baptismal certificate or record (including copies or certified records)
- The baptism must have taken place within a reasonable time after the birth.
- census records
- boat manifest
- birth certificate from another country that shows the parent-child relationship in each generation

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
hits.text:
If you were born and adopted outside Canada
If you were born outside Canada and adopted by a Canadian parent, you’re not automatically a Canadian citizen.
Before submitting an application, learn about citizenship by descent for adopted people .
Minors who are permanent residents
If your minor child is a permanent resident, you will likely need to apply for your child’s Canadian citizenship (naturalization or grant of citizenship) to get a citizenship certificate.
If you apply to become a Canadian citizen
If you apply for and receive Canadian citizenship ( naturalization or grant of citizenship ), you
- will receive the certificate at a citizenship ceremony
- do not need to apply for a citizenship certificate

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
hits.text:
Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: Who can apply
- 1. About the process
- 2. Who can apply
- 3. How to apply
- 4. After you apply
Who this application is for
If you’re already a Canadian citizen, you may want to apply for a citizenship certificate if you want to
- have a document that proves your Canadian citizenship (such as to apply for a passport, job, pension or social insurance number)
- replace a lost, destroyed or stolen certificate
- update your certificate, such as when you get a legal name change
If you don’t know if you’re a Canadian citizen or not, you can apply for a citizenship certificate to find out for sure.
If you’re a parent, you may also want to apply on behalf of a minor child who was born outside Canada.

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
hits.text:
If you need urgent processing
We may be able to process your application faster in some cases.
You need to apply on paper
You need to apply on paper if
- you were born in Canada on or before February 14, 1977
- you became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or before April 16, 2009
- you were born outside of Canada to a parent who
- was born in Canada on or before February 16, 1977, or
- became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or before April 16, 2009
- you’re applying for minors (under 18) for whom you’re the legal guardian
- you or a minor was born in Canada
- you need to replace or update your certificate
- you’re applying for 2 to 3 children and only some of them are naturalized Canadian citizens
- you’re applying for 4 or more children
- you’re applying for a replacement certificate for yourself and your children
- you don’t know information about your parents or grandparents
- For example, you don’t know when your parent was born or if your grandparent was a crown servant.

hits.text:
If you’re applying for yourself
You can apply online if you were born on or after February 15, 1977, and you
- became a naturalized Canadian citizen on or after April 17, 2009, or
- were born outside of Canada to a parent who was:
- born in Canada on or after February 15, 1977, or

hits.text:
DND 419 birth certificates
They were issued by the Department of National Defence to children born outside Canada to Canadian Forces personnel before November 1979.
If you need a proof of Canadian citizenship
If you’re a Canadian citizen who doesn’t have a valid proof of citizenship, you can apply for a citizenship certificate .

hits.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate: How to apply
hits.text:
Permanent resident minors: You need to apply for the child’s Canadian citizenship

- Do not apply directly for a citizenship certificate (online or on paper). If you do, we’ll return your application.
Getting a certificate for the first time: You can’t apply together with an adopted child who was born outside Canada
You cannot apply for yourself and an adopted child (under 18) born outside Canada at the same time (online or on paper).

question: How do I print an electronic citizenship certificate so that it remains valid?

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
How to print an e-certificate
If you need to print the e-certificate, you must do it in a certain way for it to be a valid document.
To do this, you must print both pages
- on letter size (8.5 x 11 inches) paper
- in colour or black ink
- in portrait orientation
The information on the printed certificate must be
- legible (clear and easy to read)
- fully visible (not cut-off)
You can choose
- the type of printer paper (such as photocopy paper or cardstock)
- to print it double-sided or not
- You can print on 2 pieces of paper and staple them (check the instructions for your application to be sure).
If you print an e-certificate, do not photocopy or laminate it. If you do, the certificate will become invalid .

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
What you can do with an e-certificate
You can view and download your e-certificate as many times as you want. After downloading an e-certificate, you can
- save it to any device (desktop, laptop, tablet or mobile phone)
- print it as many times you want
- use it to apply for various services and benefits
Valid formats of the e-certificate
The e-certificate is always a valid proof of citizenship even when you
- print it
- display it on your device
- send it as a file attachment
When applying for a service, benefit or job, you must follow the requirements for that application.
- File type: Some applications may ask you to provide your e-certificate in a specific format like jpg or png.
- Passport: If you apply for a new adult passport , you must print your e-certificate.
- Social insurance number (SIN):
- You can apply online for your SIN using your e-certificate.
- If you apply in person , you must print your e-certificate. You can get your SIN the same day.

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
Get your e-certificate authenticated
Authentication is the process used to confirm that your e-certificate is valid and that the document is genuine.
You may need to get your e-certificate authenticated if
- you’re outside Canada and
- you need assistance or service from a foreign embassy, high commissioner or consulate
If you need your e-certificate authenticated, you must print it first .
Learn more about authenticating a document.
Contact us
How you contact us depends on your issue and what you applied for:

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
You get the message “ Information you provided does not correspond with our database ”
Double check that you entered your information correctly, including your date of birth, UCI and application number. If you’re downloading someone else’s certificate, you must enter their information, not your own.
If you entered your information correctly and it still doesn’t work, contact us .
Don’t apply to replace your e-certificate
If you still have issues with your e-certificate after trying the solutions above, don’t apply to replace your certificate.
Contact us through our web form instead.

hits.title: Learn more about the electronic citizenship certificate
hits.text:
Online application for a citizenship certificate (proof of citizenship)
In most cases, you’ll get the letter in your IRCC secure account .
- If you asked us to communicate with you through email after you applied, we’ll send the letter to the last email address you gave us .
- If you applied with the help of a representative, we’ll email them the letter .
If you applied with the help of a representative
Your representative will receive the letter with instructions on how to download your e-certificate.
To download your e-certificate without going through your representative, use this page to create your own IRCC Portal account .
You may still ask your representative to forward you the instructions letter.
- Do not use the invite code in the letter. You must request a new invitation code using your own email in the IRCC portal.
- The letter has other helpful information about your e-certificate, such as where in the IRCC Portal you can download the file.

hits.text:
After we process your application
If your application is approved
You receive your Canadian citizenship certificate by mail.
If your application is not approved
You receive a letter that explains why your application was refused.
Check and update your application
You can check your application status online only after you’ve received an acknowledgement of receipt (AOR) letter or email.

Learn how to understand your application status .
We may contact you to get more information if your case is non-routine .
Check your application status

hits.title: International Experience Canada: About the program
hits.text:
Text displays: “Monitor your Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) account while you wait”
An applicant checks their email, including their junk mail folder. An applicant uploads a document, hits the “Next” button, scrolls down to the “Signature” section and then hits the “Transmit” button. In the table of documents, the word “Provided” is highlighted.
Make sure you check your email and junk mail folders, as you might be asked for more documents. After uploading more documents, make sure you press “Next”, provide an electronic signature and then press “Transmit”. It should say “Provided” next to the document you’ve uploaded.

hits.title: Find out if you have the language proof for citizenship: Step 3
hits.text:
Did you complete LINC (Language Instruction for Newcomers to Canada) training? Or the Cours de langue pour les immigrants au Canada (CLIC)?
If you did , you need to have a Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB) Level 4 or higher in speaking and listening.
- If you did your training on or after November 1, 2012 , submit a copy of your certificate with your application.
- If you did you training between January 2008 and October 2012 , mark the box on your application. We’ll verify it electronically.

hits.title: Check if you may be a citizen
hits.text:
How to confirm if you’re a Canadian citizen
You can apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate if you
- don’t have proof of your Canadian citizenship
- lost your documents or they were stolen
- are not sure if you’re a Canadian citizen and want us to check
This proof will help you apply for a Canadian passport and avoid delays at the border if you plan to enter Canada .
We’ll review your application to check if you’re a Canadian citizen. If you are, we’ll issue you a citizenship certificate (proof of your Canadian citizenship). This certificate is valid proof that you’re a citizen.
Apply for a citizenship certificate .

hits.title: Find out if you have the language proof for citizenship: Step 2
hits.text:
Your test date: On or before March 31, 2014
To apply for Canadian citizenship, your results need to be:
2H or higher (3L, 3H, 4L, 4H, 5L, or 5H) in listening and speaking
If your results are high enough , include a copy of your test results (even if they’re expired) with your citizenship application.
If your results are not high enough , find other language proof you can submit .
Your test date: On or after April 1, 2014
To apply for Canadian citizenship, your results need to be:
4 or higher (up to 12) in listening and speaking
If your results are high enough , include a copy of your test results (even if they’re expired) with your citizenship application.
If your results are not high enough , find other language proof you can submit .

question: Can I book my citizenship test myself if the time between the start and end dates in my invitation is not 30 days?

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
You must wait until you receive your invitation before you can take the test. You can’t book the test yourself or contact us to get an invitation. We’ll send the invitation as quickly as possible.
You can check your application status to confirm that your invitation is on its way. When you check, go to the “Citizenship test” section of the status tracker. The In progress status means that
- we have scheduled your test
- you’ll get your invitation soon
Check your application status

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
Online test only: If the time between the start and end dates in your invitation is not 30 days
If the time between the start date and the end date of your test is not 30 days, email us
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- a screenshot or attachment of your test invitation
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
Use the email address we provided in your invitation.
When you’ll get a test invitation
Most people get the invitation 1 to 3 months after they receive the acknowledgment of receipt of their application (AOR).
The wait time for an invitation also depends on your situation and our current processing times. For example, you may wait longer if your application is non-routine .
You must wait until you receive your invitation before you can take the test. You can’t book the test yourself or contact us to get an invitation. We’ll send the invitation as quickly as possible.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
When you can take the test
If you take the test online , you can take your test only between the start date and end date provided on your invitation. This will be a 30-day period.
After you receive your invitation, you
- have up to 3 chances to pass the test during the 30-day period
- If you fail, log in and try again to use your chances.
- can take the test at any time during the 30-day period (including weekends and holidays)
You can’t sign in to the test
- before or after the 30-day period on your invitation or
- after you submit the test

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
Wait for a test invitation
You need an invitation to take the test online.
What’s on the invitation
We’ll send you an invitation by email to take the online test after you submit your citizenship application. The test invitation is a PDF attachment in an email. The PDF includes instructions on what to do before, during and after the test.
Your invitation should have
- a test start date and end date (you’ll have 30 days to take it)
- a link to the test (or directions for an in-person test)
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
- an email address you can use to contact us

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
If you haven’t received an invitation by the start date in the status tracker
If your application status says you’ve been scheduled for an online test, but you haven’t received an invitation yet, you should get it soon. They usually arrive at least 2 to 3 business days before your test start date.
If it’s less than 2 to 3 business days before the start date, send an an email to IRCC.CitOnlineTest-TestenligneCit-IRCC@cic.gc.ca with
- a detailed explanation of the issue
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)

hits.title: Citizenship test: If you missed the test
hits.text:
If you missed the test
Find out what to do if you didn’t take the test either during the 30-day period provided in your invitation or when it was scheduled.
You missed your first test the first time we invited you
If this is the first time we invited you, but you missed the test, we’ll automatically send you a new invitation. You still have 3 chances to pass the test within the new 30-day period.
You missed a second test invitation
If this is the second time we invited you, and you didn’t take your test, email the address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation and provide
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
If you missed the test twice and didn’t contact us, we’ll abandon (stop processing) your application. You’ll have to start the application process over if you want to apply for citizenship again.

hits.title: Citizenship test: If you missed the test
hits.text:
You missed your first test
If this was the first time we invited you to the test and you missed it, you have 2 options:
- contact us
- wait for us to reschedule your test
Option 1: Contact us (recommended)
Send an explanation within 30 days of your missed test date to the email address in the “Rescheduling” section of your test invitation. In your email, include
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule the test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
You can also send your explanation by mail to the office that scheduled your test if you don’t have an email address. Check your test invitation for the address of that office.
We’ll use the postmark date on your envelope as the date you sent your explanation.
After you contact us, we’ll send you a new invitation.
- If your reason is valid, the new invitation will count as your first invitation.
- If your reason is invalid, the new invitation will count as your final invitation.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Test results and next steps
hits.text:
Official test result
For tests taken in person and on Microsoft Teams , you’ll get your official test score right after you take the test.
After you take the online test , one of our officers will review your result to make it official. This could take a few days or a few weeks. There are 3 possible test results:
Pass
You correctly answered at least 15 of the 20 questions (75%).
Fail
You failed all your test attempts during the 30-day period in your invitation.
Invalidated
Your test result may be invalid if
- we find out or suspect that you cheated
- a technical issue prevents us from confirming your identity or your test score

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Take the online test
After you receive the invitation, you can take the online citizenship test. Find out what you need to do to prepare for and complete the test.
This page doesn’t apply to the other test formats (in person or on Microsoft Teams).
Getting ready for the test
Citizenship tests are 45 minutes long. Once the timer starts, you won’t be able to stop it. After 45 minutes, your test will be submitted automatically, even if you’re not finished. You’ll get a warning when you have 5 minutes left.
Before you start the test, make sure you’re prepared.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
403 error message
If you get a 403 error message when you sign in, try
- turning off your virtual private network (VPN)
- disabling your browser extensions
- using a different device
- using a different Internet connection
- waiting a few hours to take the test
If you still have issues signing in, email the address in your test invitation.
“You can’t take the test right now” message
You may see this message if you
- attempted to sign in
- before you got your test invitation
- before or after your 30-day period of test access
- entered the wrong application number or unique client identifier (UCI)
If you still have issues signing in, email the address in your test invitation.

question: Can I apply to resume my Canadian citizenship urgently if I need to travel due to a serious illness in my family and cannot get a passport in my current nationality?

hits.title: Apply to resume your citizenship urgently
hits.text:
Apply to resume your citizenship urgently
We can only process requests to resume Canadian citizenship urgently in special cases. Every urgent request will be checked to see if it meets the conditions for urgent processing. If an application does not meet the conditions, it will be processed normally.
To apply for urgent processing, you must meet all the conditions to resume your Canadian citizenship .
Examples of when we may process an application for resumption of citizenship urgently:
- You can't apply for a job or could lose your job because you are not a Canadian citizen.
- You cannot go to a Canadian school, college or university because you are not a Canadian citizen.
- You need to travel because of death or serious illness in the family and cannot get a passport in your current nationality.
- You received a decision on a previous application for citizenship that you successfully appealed to the Federal Court.

hits.text:
How to request faster processing of your work permit extension if you need to travel urgently
If we’re still processing your work permit extension application, and you need to travel outside Canada urgently, you may be able to request urgent processing so you can continue to work in Canada when you return.
If you submit an incomplete request (for example, you’re missing documents), your application won’t be processed urgently.
Who can request urgent processing
You can request urgent processing if you meet all the criteria listed below:
- You applied for a work permit from within Canada before your initial work permit expired.
- You’re currently authorized to work in Canada without a work permit while we process your application.
- You must be travelling for 1 of these reasons :
- business travel that cannot be delayed
- a death in the family
- a serious illness in the family

- Select, Update your application (for example, submit documents) .
- Select, Add a document to your application .

First-time applicants
If this is the first time you have applied for citizenship, you will need to send the original or a clear and easily readable certified copy of the required documents.

Wait for a decision
Learn what happens after you submit your application and how you can track its status.
What happens first
When the Case Processing Centre in Sydney (CPC Sydney) receives your application, the staff there will check that you
- included all the required documents
- paid the correct fees
If your application is complete , we’ll start processing your application and send you an acknowledgement of receipt letter.
If your application is incomplete or missing fees, we’ll return your application to you.
After the initial review, CPC Sydney sends your application to a local IRCC office to make a final decision. You may be asked to attend an interview with a citizenship officer or a citizenship judge.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
- If you sent yourself a test link multiple times, use the latest test link to sign in.
- Confirm your identity
- Re-enter your application number and UCI to confirm your identity.
- Take photos of your identification (ID) and yourself
- Your ID can be your permanent resident (PR) card or a valid piece of ID with your photo and signature on it (for example, a driver’s licence or health card).
- Wear appropriate clothing for your photo. You may wear traditional or religious clothing, head coverings, and reading or prescription glasses, but your face must be clearly visible.
- If your photos look blurred, your test may be invalid, and we may ask you to take the test again.
- Start the test
- When you’re ready to start the test, select the “Start the test” button. The 45-minute countdown will begin.
Go to the test

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Taking clear photos
Your photos must be clear and easy to see. Make sure that the information on your ID is easy to read.
If either the photo of your personal ID or of your face is unclear
- move your ID closer to the webcam
- change your webcam setting or brightness
- adjust the lighting of you test location or
- use a different device
If we can’t clearly see your photos, your test result may be invalid, and you may have to take the test again.
Accidentally taking a photo of your face instead of your identification (ID)
If you accidentally took a picture of your face instead of your photo ID, you don’t have to contact us. We’ll review your test result and contact you with your next steps.
Depending on the result of our review, your test result may be invalid, and we may send you a new invitation. If you have to take the test again, it can take a few weeks or months to schedule it.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
Pick a good test location
The test location must have good lighting so our system can see you clearly through your webcam. You can take the test in a public library or with a public computer.
You don’t need to be in Canada to take the online test.
Taking the test
While you’re taking your citizenship test, we’ll use your webcam to take random photos to confirm your identity and ensure you’re working alone. We’ll compare these photos with your test photo and the ones from your application.
If there are technical issues or signs of cheating, your test may be invalid. We’ll follow up and ask you to take the test again.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Take the online test
hits.text:
What to do and not to do during the test
To avoid having to retake the test for a technical reason, make sure you
- turn on your webcam and check that your face is fully visible in the frame
- have a reliable Internet connection
- have no other tabs, windows or programs open on the computer
- turn off your virtual private network (VPN)
- give yourself enough time to take the test (because the timer can’t be paused)
For your test to be valid, you must
- take the test alone
- take the test in the same place you took the photo of yourself and your ID before the test
- make sure there are no items in the background that have your personal information on them (like a diploma)
There are also some things you must not do during the test:
- Don’t use any other devices.
- Don’t look at any study materials.
- Don’t use the back button in your web browser.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
Wait for a test invitation
You need an invitation to take the test online.
What’s on the invitation
We’ll send you an invitation by email to take the online test after you submit your citizenship application. The test invitation is a PDF attachment in an email. The PDF includes instructions on what to do before, during and after the test.
Your invitation should have
- a test start date and end date (you’ll have 30 days to take it)
- a link to the test (or directions for an in-person test)
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
- an email address you can use to contact us

hits.title: Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
hits.text:
Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
When you apply for citizenship, you can request an accommodation for certain requirements if you need it for accessibility or another reason.
An accommodation will help you to meet a citizenship requirement, such as the citizenship test, ceremony, or language hearing.
Types of accommodation
Here are some of the accommodations you can request:
Medical, physiological, psychological or cognitive conditions (including disabilities)
Depending on your situation, we can give you
- a Braille, large-print, or oral version of the test
- more time to take the test
- wheelchair access at an in-person test or ceremony
- sign-language interpretation at a citizenship ceremony or a language hearing
You may bring your own personal assistance, such as
- a care attendant
- a service animal
- a sighted guide
We may also invite you to take the test or go to the ceremony in person.

hits.title: Accessibility accommodations for citizenship application
hits.text:
If you cannot take the test online
We may invite you to take the test in person or with Microsoft Teams if you
- have a weak or unreliable Internet connection
- have no access to an electronic device or webcam
- cannot use the supported browsers for the test (Chrome or Safari)
Face covering (online test)
Your face must be fully visible through your webcam during the online test.
We may invite you to take the test in person or with Microsoft Teams if you can’t remove your face covering.
Ceremony accommodations
We may invite you to a virtual or an in-person ceremony.

hits.title: Citizenship test: Wait for a test invitation
hits.text:
If you’re taking the test in person or on Microsoft Teams
If you take the test in person or on Microsoft Teams, your invitation will include the details, for example, the time and location. If you fail the test, you’ll get a new invitation for another time.
How to reschedule the test
If you need to reschedule the test, email the address in the rescheduling section of your test invitation. In your email, include
- a detailed explanation of why you need to reschedule your test
- your application number
- your unique client identifier (UCI)
It usually takes 4 to 8 weeks to reschedule your test, but it may take longer.
Urgent processing for emergencies
If you need to take the test before the 30-day period on your invitation due to an emergency, check if you qualify for urgent processing .

hits.title: Citizenship test: Test results and next steps
hits.text:
What to expect if you’re invited to an interview
We may invite you to an interview to
- verify your identity
- authenticate photocopies of your documents
- verify if you’re eligible for Canadian citizenship
Interviews will not necessarily result in a final decision.
When you come for your interview, bring
- the original documents you sent with your application
- any passport or travel documents you used in the 5 years before you applied
If you fail the test
Within your 30-day test period, you have up to 3 chances to pass the test (whether online, on Microsoft Teams, or in person).
If you fail the test all 3 times, we’ll invite you to a hearing with a citizenship official.

When you’ll get a test invitation
Most people get the invitation 1 to 3 months after they receive the acknowledgment of receipt of their application (AOR).

If your Canadian company is inviting a visitor, a representative of the company should write the letter. Some firms have specific people who sign letters of invitation. Your company should send each visitor two originals of the letter of invitation, one for them to submit when applying for their visa and one to present when they enter Canada.
Be sure to leave enough time for your visitor’s visa to be processed. See the application processing times to find out how long it may take to process a visa.

- about the person being invited
